test_cases.test_inputs: New linking information (non-infill) with a reference balise group BG2 (where BG1 < BG2).

steps.action: Receive new linking information (non-infill) with reference balise group BG2.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces all stored linking information from BG2 onwards. The linking information associated with BG1 remains unchanged.

steps.action: Query the stored linking information for the reference balise group BG1.
steps.expected: The original linking information for BG1 is still stored.

steps.action: Query the stored linking information for the reference balise group BG2.
steps.expected: The new linking information for BG2 is stored.

test_cases.title: Replacement of linking information (infill) from infill reference location
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored linking information. The train is located before the infill reference location (balise group at next main signal).
test_cases.test_inputs: New linking information (infill) with an infill reference location BG3.

steps.action: Receive new linking information (infill) with infill reference location BG3.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces all stored linking information from BG3 onwards. The linking information before BG3 remains unchanged.

steps.action: Query the stored linking information for the infill reference location BG3.
steps.expected: The new infill linking information is stored for BG3.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for PBD speed restrictions on trackside request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored Speed Restriction to ensure Permitted Braking Distance (PBD) information for a track section. The train is located before the start of this restriction.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trackside request to resume initial state for PBD speed restrictions beyond a given location L_req.

steps.action: Receive a trackside request to resume initial state for PBD speed restrictions beyond location L_req.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for the stored PBD speed restriction information beyond location L_req.

steps.action: Query the stored PBD speed restriction information beyond L_req.
steps.expected: The PBD speed restriction information beyond L_req is in its initial state (e.g., no restriction or default value).

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for axle load speed profiles on trackside request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored axle load speed profile information for a track section. The train is located before the start of this profile.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trackside request to resume initial state for axle load speed profiles beyond a given location L_req.

steps.action: Receive a trackside request to resume initial state for axle load speed profiles beyond location L_req.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for the stored axle load speed profile information beyond location L_req.

steps.action: Query the stored axle load speed profile information beyond L_req.
steps.expected: The axle load speed profile information beyond L_req is in its initial state.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for grouped track condition types on single request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored track condition information for types: sound horn, non stopping area, tunnel stopping area, powerless section – lower pantograph, powerless section – switch off the main power switch, radio hole, air tightness, switch off regenerative brake, switch off eddy current brake for service brake, switch off eddy current brake for emergency brake, and switch off magnetic shoe brake. The train is located before the start of these conditions.
test_cases.test_inputs: Single trackside request to resume initial state for the listed track condition types beyond a given location L_req.

steps.action: Receive a single trackside request to resume initial state for the listed track condition types beyond location L_req.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for all the listed track condition types beyond location L_req.

steps.action: Query the stored track condition information for each of the listed types beyond L_req.
steps.expected: All listed track condition types beyond L_req are in their initial state.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for route suitability data on single request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored route suitability information (loading gauge, traction system, axle load). The train is located before the start of this information.
test_cases.test_inputs: Single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored route suitability information beyond a given location L_req.

steps.action: Receive a single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored route suitability information beyond location L_req.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for all stored route suitability information beyond location L_req.

steps.action: Query the stored route suitability information beyond L_req.
steps.expected: All route suitability information beyond L_req is in its initial state.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for Station Platform track conditions on single request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored track condition information of the type Station Platform. The train is located before the start of this information.
test_cases.test_inputs: Single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored track condition information of the type Station Platform beyond a given location L_req.

steps.action: Receive a single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored track condition information of the type Station Platform beyond location L_req.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for the stored Station Platform track condition information beyond location L_req.

steps.action: Query the stored Station Platform track condition information beyond L_req.
steps.expected: The Station Platform track condition information beyond L_req is in its initial state.

test_cases.title: Supervised Manoeuvre with same validity direction as train orientation
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where location based information is stored. The train is oriented in direction D1. Location based information is stored for direction D1.
test_cases.test_inputs: Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with validity direction D1 (same as current train orientation).

steps.action: Receive a Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with validity direction D1.
steps.expected: The OBU applies the normal replacement rules of SUBSET-026 §3.7.3.1. The previously stored location based information is replaced according to these rules, not deleted entirely.

steps.action: Query the stored location based information.
steps.expected: The location based information is updated according to the replacement rules, and some previous information may still be stored if not replaced.

test_cases.title: Supervised Manoeuvre with opposite validity direction to train orientation
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where location based information is stored. The train is oriented in direction D1. Location based information is stored for direction D1.
test_cases.test_inputs: Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with validity direction D2 (opposite to current train orientation D1).

steps.action: Receive a Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with validity direction D2.
steps.expected: The OBU does not apply the normal replacement rules. Instead, it deletes all previously stored location based information.

steps.action: Query the stored location based information.
steps.expected: All previously stored location based information is deleted. No location based information from the previous orientation remains.

test_cases.title: MA request includes all applicable reasons when multiple triggers occur simultaneously
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC. Train is in a mode where MA requests are allowed (e.g., FS). A perturbation location is defined such that the train front is currently passing the calculated trigger location. Simultaneously, the Section timer for the current MA is about to expire such that the defined time-before-expiration criterion is met.
test_cases.assumptions: The RBC is configured to accept MA requests. The train speed and position are such that both the perturbation location criterion and the Section timer criterion are fulfilled at the same instant.

steps.action: Allow the train to reach the point where the train front passes the location defined by the perturbation criterion and the time-before-Section-timer-expiration criterion is met simultaneously.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the sent MA request message.
steps.expected: The MA request contains both the reason 'Time before reaching the perturbation location reached' and the reason 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request includes 'Start' reason and existing timer reason
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. Train is at standstill. The Section timer for the current MA is running and the defined time-before-expiration criterion is met. The driver is ready to select 'Start'.

steps.action: Driver selects 'Start' on the DMI.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the sent MA request message.
steps.expected: The MA request contains the reason 'Start selected by driver' and the reason 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request triggered by passing perturbation location
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC defining the time-before-perturbation-location. A perturbation location is defined in the track description. The train is running at a speed such that the calculated trigger location (defined time before perturbation location at warning speed) is ahead of the train front.
test_cases.assumptions: The train is running at or below the warning speed associated with the perturbation location for the calculation of the trigger point.

steps.action: Drive the train so that the train front passes the location calculated as the defined time before the perturbation location.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Time before reaching the perturbation location reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request triggered by Section timer criterion
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC defining the time-before-Section-timer-expiration. The train has an MA with a Section timer that is running. The train is in a mode where the Section timer is supervised.

steps.action: Wait until the time remaining on the Section timer equals the defined time-before-expiration value specified in the MA request parameters.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request triggered by LOA speed timer criterion
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC defining the time-before-LOA-speed-timer-expiration. The train has an MA with a LOA speed timer that is running (e.g., due to a temporary EOA or specific speed restriction).

steps.action: Wait until the time remaining on the LOA speed timer equals the defined time-before-expiration value specified in the MA request parameters.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request triggered by track description deletion (valid situation)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. The OBU has stored track description information. A situation occurs that causes part of the track description to be deleted according to SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4, specifically a situation that is NOT a, b, f, or k (e.g., deletion due to reception of a new MA that overwrites old track description, or deletion due to train passing a location where track description is no longer valid).
test_cases.assumptions: The specific deletion situation is one of the valid triggers listed in A.3.4 excluding a, b, f, k.

steps.action: Trigger a track description deletion event that falls under a valid situation in A.3.4 (excluding a, b, f, k).
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Track description deletion'.

test_cases.title: No MA request triggered by track description deletion (excluded situation a)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. The OBU has stored track description information. A situation occurs that causes part of the track description to be deleted according to situation 'a' of SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4.
test_cases.assumptions: Situation 'a' in A.3.4 is an excluded case for triggering MA requests.

steps.action: Trigger a track description deletion event that falls under situation 'a' in A.3.4.
steps.expected: The OBU does NOT send an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Track description deletion'.

test_cases.title: No MA request triggered by track description deletion (excluded situation b)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. The OBU has stored track description information. A situation occurs that causes part of the track description to be deleted according to situation 'b' of SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4.
test_cases.assumptions: Situation 'b' in A.3.4 is an excluded case for triggering MA requests.

steps.action: Trigger a track description deletion event that falls under situation 'b' in A.3.4.
steps.expected: The OBU does NOT send an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Track description deletion'.

test_cases.title: No MA request triggered by track description deletion (excluded situation f)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. The OBU has stored track description information. A situation occurs that causes part of the track description to be deleted according to situation 'f' of SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4.
test_cases.assumptions: Situation 'f' in A.3.4 is an excluded case for triggering MA requests.

steps.action: Trigger a track description deletion event that falls under situation 'f' in A.3.4.
steps.expected: The OBU does NOT send an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Track description deletion'.

test_cases.title: No MA request triggered by track description deletion (excluded situation k)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. The OBU has stored track description information. A situation occurs that causes part of the track description to be deleted according to situation 'k' of SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4.
test_cases.assumptions: Situation 'k' in A.3.4 is an excluded case for triggering MA requests.

steps.action: Trigger a track description deletion event that falls under situation 'k' in A.3.4.
steps.expected: The OBU does NOT send an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Track description deletion'.

test_cases.title: End Section timer start upon passing start location
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in a mode where MA is active (e.g., FS). An MA with an End Section timer start location is stored. The train's max safe front end is located just before the End Section timer start location.

steps.action: Move the train forward so that its max safe front end passes the End Section timer start location.
steps.expected: The End Section timer starts counting.

test_cases.title: End Section timer timeout consequences
test_cases.preconditions: End Section timer is running. The current MA has a non-zero target speed at the End of Movement Authority (LOA). Location based information per Appendix A.3.4 is stored.
test_cases.assumptions: Time can be accelerated or the timeout value is set to a short duration for testing.

steps.action: Wait until the End Section timer value exceeds the time-out value given by trackside.
steps.expected: The EOA/LOA is withdrawn to the train's current position. The location based information listed in Appendix A.3.4 is deleted. The target speed at the End of Movement Authority is set to zero.

test_cases.title: LOA speed timer start in Level 2
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2 operation. Communication session with RBC is established. Train is in FS mode.

steps.action: Receive a new MA message from the RBC containing a non-zero LOA speed.
steps.expected: The LOA speed timer starts at the time stamp of the received message.

test_cases.title: LOA speed timer start in Level 1
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 operation. Train is in FS mode. A balise group providing an MA with a non-zero LOA speed is ahead.

steps.action: Pass the first encountered balise of the balise group that gives the MA.
steps.expected: The LOA speed timer starts at the moment of passing the first balise.

test_cases.title: LOA speed timer timeout consequences
test_cases.preconditions: LOA speed timer is running. The current MA has a non-zero target speed at the End of Movement Authority (LOA).
test_cases.assumptions: Time can be accelerated or the timeout value is set to a short duration for testing.

steps.action: Wait until the LOA speed timer value exceeds the time-out value received from trackside.
steps.expected: The speed associated with the LOA is set to zero. The LOA becomes an EOA. The Supervised Location is determined per §3.8.4.5. Location based information listed in Appendix A.3.4 is deleted accordingly.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer start upon passing start location
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in a mode where MA is active. An MA with an Overlap timer start location and a finite time-out value is stored. The train's max safe front end is located just before the Overlap timer start location.

steps.action: Move the train forward so that its max safe front end passes the Overlap timer start location.
steps.expected: The Overlap timer starts counting.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer start with infinite time-out value
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in a mode where MA is active. An MA with an Overlap timer start location and a time-out value of 'infinite' is stored. The train's max safe front end is located just before the Overlap timer start location.

steps.action: Move the train forward so that its max safe front end passes the Overlap timer start location.
steps.expected: The Overlap timer is considered as started.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer timeout consequences
test_cases.preconditions: Overlap timer is running. The current MA includes an overlap with a release speed and a non-zero target speed at the End of Movement Authority.
test_cases.assumptions: Time can be accelerated or the timeout value is set to a short duration for testing.

steps.action: Wait until the Overlap timer value exceeds the time-out value given by trackside.
steps.expected: The overlap information is deleted. The release speed associated with the Overlap is deleted. The Supervised Location is redetermined per §3.8.4.5. Location based information per Appendix A.3.4 is deleted. The target speed at the End of Movement Authority is set to zero.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer expiration upon train standstill
test_cases.preconditions: Overlap timer has been started. The train is moving. The current MA includes an overlap.

steps.action: Bring the train to a standstill after the Overlap timer has been started.
steps.expected: The OBU considers the Overlap timer value as greater than its time-out value. The consequences defined in §3.8.4.4.2 are applied: overlap deleted, release speed deleted, SvL redetermined, target speed at EOA set to zero.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer expiration upon receiving new MA with rear start location
test_cases.preconditions: No Overlap timer is currently running. The train's max safe front end is at a specific position. A new MA is received with an Overlap timer start location located in rear of the train's max safe front end.

steps.action: Receive the new MA with the Overlap timer start location in rear of the max safe front end.
steps.expected: The OBU considers that the Overlap timer value has exceeded its time-out value. The consequences defined in §3.8.4.4.2 are applied: overlap deleted, release speed deleted, SvL redetermined, target speed at EOA set to zero.

test_cases.title: Supervised Location determination with valid Overlap
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in FS mode. An MA is active with an Overlap that has not timed out. A Danger Point and an End Section are also defined in the MA.

steps.action: Check the Supervised Location (SvL) determined by the OBU.
steps.expected: The SvL is set to the end of the overlap.

test_cases.title: Supervised Location determination with timed-out Overlap and valid Danger Point
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in FS mode. An MA is active. The Overlap has timed out (or does not exist). A Danger Point is defined in the MA. An End Section is also defined.

steps.action: Check the Supervised Location (SvL) determined by the OBU.
steps.expected: The SvL is set to the Danger Point.

test_cases.title: Supervised Location determination with no Overlap or Danger Point
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in FS mode. An MA is active. No Overlap exists (or it has timed out). No Danger Point is defined in the MA. An End Section is defined.

steps.action: Check the Supervised Location (SvL) determined by the OBU.
steps.expected: The SvL is set to the end of the End Section.

test_cases.title: Infill MA evaluation in FS mode
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 or Level 2. Train is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. Linking information for the relevant main signal balise group is available.

steps.action: Receive an infill MA.
steps.expected: The OBU evaluates the infill MA.

test_cases.title: Infill MA evaluation in AD mode
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 or Level 2. Train is in Automatic Driving (AD) mode. Linking information for the relevant main signal balise group is available.

steps.action: Receive an infill MA.
steps.expected: The OBU evaluates the infill MA.

test_cases.title: Infill MA evaluation in LS mode
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 or Level 2. Train is in Limited Supervision (LS) mode. Linking information for the relevant main signal balise group is available.

test_cases.test_inputs: A new MA from RBC defining an SvL at a location closer to the train than the current LOA.

steps.action: Receive a new MA from the RBC that defines an SvL at a location closer to the train than the current LOA.
steps.expected: The OBU treats the new MA as an MA shortening. The OBU deletes the stored location based information listed in SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4 that is beyond the new SvL.

test_cases.title: Repositioning information is not treated as MA shortening
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1, train in FS, a valid MA is currently supervised. Linking information announces a following balise group as unknown but containing repositioning information.
test_cases.test_inputs: Repositioning information contained in a balise group message.

steps.action: Receive repositioning information from a balise group message that updates the length of the current MA section.
steps.expected: The OBU updates the length of the current MA section. The OBU does not treat this reception as an MA shortening, so no location based information is deleted.

test_cases.title: New MA ending with LOA is not treated as MA shortening
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, train in FS, a valid MA ending with an SvL is currently supervised. Location based information is stored beyond the SvL.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new MA from RBC ending with an LOA.

steps.action: Receive a new MA from the RBC that ends with an LOA, replacing the previous MA that ended with an SvL.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces the previous MA with the new MA. The OBU does not treat this reception as an MA shortening, so the stored location based information beyond the new LOA is not deleted.

test_cases.title: Acceptance of MA shortening when train is in rear of Indication supervision limit
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session with RBC established, train running in a mode with valid MA (e.g., FS). The current MA has an EOA/LOA at a known distance. The RBC is ready to send a 'Request to shorten MA'.
test_cases.test_inputs: RBC sends a 'Request to shorten MA' with a proposed shortened MA where the Indication supervision limit is located 100 m ahead of the current train front end position.

steps.action: The RBC sends a 'Request to shorten MA' containing a proposed shortened MA with an Indication supervision limit located 100 m ahead of the current train front end position.
steps.expected: The OBU checks the train front end position against the Indication supervision limit. Since the train is in rear, the OBU accepts the request.

steps.action: The OBU updates its internal state with the new MA.
steps.expected: The OBU adopts the proposed shortened MA as the new MA. If the request included a mode profile or SH-area balise group list, these are also stored and applied.

steps.action: The OBU sends a response to the RBC.
steps.expected: The OBU informs the RBC that the request to shorten the MA has been accepted.

test_cases.title: Rejection of MA shortening when train is in advance of Indication supervision limit
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session with RBC established, train running in a mode with valid MA (e.g., FS). The current MA has an EOA/LOA at a known distance. The RBC is ready to send a 'Request to shorten MA'.
test_cases.test_inputs: RBC sends a 'Request to shorten MA' with a proposed shortened MA where the Indication supervision limit is located 50 m behind the current train front end position.

steps.action: The RBC sends a 'Request to shorten MA' containing a proposed shortened MA with an Indication supervision limit located 50 m behind the current train front end position.
steps.expected: The OBU checks the train front end position against the Indication supervision limit. Since the train is in advance, the OBU rejects the request.

steps.action: The OBU maintains its internal state.
steps.expected: The OBU keeps the previously received MA, mode profile (if any), and list of balise groups for SH area (if any) valid. The new proposed MA is not adopted.

steps.action: The OBU sends a response to the RBC.
steps.expected: The OBU informs the RBC that the request to shorten the MA has been rejected.

test_cases.title: Boundary condition: Train front end exactly at Indication supervision limit
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session with RBC established, train running in a mode with valid MA (e.g., FS). The RBC is ready to send a 'Request to shorten MA'.
test_cases.test_inputs: RBC sends a 'Request to shorten MA' with a proposed shortened MA where the Indication supervision limit is exactly at the current train front end position.
test_cases.assumptions: The requirement states 'in rear' for acceptance and 'in advance' for rejection. The case 'exactly at' is interpreted as not being 'in rear' (i.e., not strictly behind), thus falling into the rejection category or requiring specific handling. Based on standard safety logic, if the limit is not strictly ahead (in rear of train), it is not safe to shorten. However, the text says 'If it is in rear... accept... If it is in advance... reject'. It does not explicitly define 'at'. Usually, 'in rear' means position < limit. 'In advance' means position > limit. If position == limit, it is not in rear. Therefore, it should be rejected to be safe, or treated as 'not in rear'. Let's assume the strict interpretation: Accept only if strictly in rear. Otherwise reject.

steps.action: The RBC sends a 'Request to shorten MA' containing a proposed shortened MA with an Indication supervision limit exactly at the current train front end position.
steps.expected: The OBU checks the train front end position. Since the train is not in rear of the limit (it is at the limit), the condition for acceptance is not met.

steps.action: The OBU processes the request.
steps.expected: The OBU rejects the request and keeps the previous MA valid.

steps.action: The OBU sends a response to the RBC.
steps.expected: The OBU informs the RBC of its decision (rejection).

test_cases.title: OBU ignores announcement for unsupported infill medium and continues with previous MA
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1, mode FS, LS or AD. The OBU is not equipped with the specific infill transmission medium requested (e.g., no Radio Infill Unit hardware or software support). A valid Movement Authority (MA) and track description are currently stored and supervised. An announcement balise group is present on the track requesting the unsupported medium.
test_cases.test_inputs: Announcement balise group data requesting an infill medium not supported by the OBU (e.g., Radio Infill).
test_cases.assumptions: The OBU's configuration explicitly excludes the requested infill medium. The previous MA allows continued movement through the test area.

steps.action: The train passes the announcement balise group that requests the unsupported infill transmission medium.
steps.expected: The OBU detects that it is not equipped with the requested medium. The OBU ignores the announcement information. No infill session is initiated. The OBU continues to supervise the train according to the previously received MA and track description without any change in permitted speed or braking intervention.

test_cases.title: OBU ignores loop infill after reading next main signal balise group
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1, mode FS, LS or AD; linking information stored (including the main signal balise group BGa); loop infill area information stored and a communication session with the loop infill unit established.

steps.action: Level 1, loop infill session established; the train passes and reads the next main signal balise group indicated in the order.
steps.expected: The OBU processes the main signal balise group and updates the MA accordingly.

steps.action: After reading the main signal balise group, the OBU receives new infill information from the loop referring to that same balise group.
steps.expected: The OBU ignores the infill information (its infill MA is not applied: no trip, no emergency brake, no change in supervision based on the ignored data).

test_cases.title: OBU ignores loop infill after detecting missed next main signal balise group
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1, mode FS, LS or AD; linking information stored (including the main signal balise group BGa with reaction 'no reaction'); loop infill area information stored and a communication session with the loop infill unit established.

steps.action: Level 1, loop infill session established; the train passes the last possible location of the next main signal balise group without reading it, triggering the 'missed' detection.
steps.expected: The OBU detects the balise group as missed and handles it according to the linking reaction (no reaction).

steps.action: After detecting the missed balise group, the OBU receives new infill information from the loop referring to that same balise group.
steps.expected: The OBU ignores the infill information (its infill MA is not applied: no trip, no emergency brake, no change in supervision based on the ignored data).

test_cases.title: Order to establish RIU session ignored when GSM-R is not installed
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is configured without a GSM-R radio system. The train is in Level 1.
test_cases.test_inputs: A balise group containing an order to establish a communication session with a specific RIU.

steps.action: The train passes a balise group that contains an order to establish a communication session with a Radio Infill Unit.
steps.expected: The OBU ignores the order. No communication session is established, and no attempt to connect to the RIU is made.

test_cases.title: Termination of existing RIU session and establishment of new one upon reaching location
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with GSM-R installed. An active communication session exists with RIU-A. The train is approaching the location specified in a new balise group order for RIU-B.
test_cases.test_inputs: A balise group order to establish a session with RIU-B, specifying a location ahead of the train.
test_cases.assumptions: The OBU is capable of handling multiple sessions or can switch sessions as per its configuration.

steps.action: The train reaches the location indicated in the balise group order for RIU-B.
steps.expected: The OBU terminates the existing communication session with RIU-A.

steps.action: The OBU attempts to establish a new communication session with RIU-B.
steps.expected: A communication session is established with RIU-B.

test_cases.title: Order via RIU ignored in degraded single-session mode
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a degraded situation where it can handle only one GSM-R communication session. An active session exists with RIU-A. The train is in Level 1.
test_cases.test_inputs: An order received via RIU-A to establish a communication session with RIU-B.

steps.action: The OBU receives an order via the active RIU-A session to establish a new session with RIU-B.
steps.expected: The OBU ignores the order. The session with RIU-A remains active, and no session is established with RIU-B.

test_cases.title: Information sent to RIU upon entering infill area and reading next main signal balise
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU. The train is approaching the location specified in a balise group order for the infill area.
test_cases.test_inputs: A balise group order specifying the entry location and the identifier of the next main signal balise group.

steps.action: The train passes the location indicated in the balise group order (entry into the infill area).
steps.expected: The OBU sends information to the RIU indicating entry into the infill area.

steps.action: The train reads the next main signal balise group indicated in the order.
steps.expected: The OBU sends information to the RIU indicating that the next main signal balise group has been read.

test_cases.title: Information sent to RIU upon detecting missed next main signal balise
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU. The train is in the infill area. The next main signal balise group is expected but not detected.
test_cases.test_inputs: A balise group order specifying the identifier of the next main signal balise group.
test_cases.assumptions: The OBU has logic to detect a missed balise based on position and time.

steps.action: The train passes the expected location of the next main signal balise group without detecting it, and the OBU detects that it was missed.
steps.expected: The OBU sends information to the RIU indicating that the next main signal balise group was missed.

test_cases.title: Content of information sent to RIU
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU. The train is entering the infill area.
test_cases.test_inputs: A balise group order specifying the entry location and the identifier of the next main signal balise group.

steps.action: The train passes the location indicated in the balise group order, triggering the OBU to send information to the RIU.
steps.expected: The message sent to the RIU contains the OBU's ETCS-ID, a position report, the identifier of the next main signal balise group, and a time stamp.

test_cases.title: Consistency check of radio infill data
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU.
test_cases.test_inputs: Radio infill data with inconsistent parameters (e.g., speed profile not matching track description or invalid MA end).
test_cases.assumptions: The specific consistency rules from SUBSET-026 §3.16.3.1 and §3.16.3.3 are implemented.

steps.action: The OBU receives radio infill data that violates the consistency principles defined in SUBSET-026 §3.16.3.1 and §3.16.3.3.
steps.expected: The OBU detects the inconsistency and rejects the data, maintaining the previous supervision state.

test_cases.title: Ignoring further radio infill information after reading next main signal balise
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU. The train has read the next main signal balise group indicated in the infill order.
test_cases.test_inputs: Further radio infill information related to the already read next main signal balise group.

steps.action: After reading the next main signal balise group, the OBU receives further radio infill information related to that balise group.
steps.expected: The OBU ignores the further radio infill information.

test_cases.title: Ignoring further radio infill information after detecting missed next main signal balise
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU. The OBU has detected that the next main signal balise group was missed.
test_cases.test_inputs: Further radio infill information related to the missed next main signal balise group.

steps.action: After detecting that the next main signal balise group was missed, the OBU receives further radio infill information related to that balise group.
steps.expected: The OBU ignores the further radio infill information.

test_cases.title: Termination of RIU session upon trackside order
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU.
test_cases.test_inputs: A termination order received from a balise group or the RIU.

steps.action: The OBU receives a termination order from trackside (balise group or RIU).
steps.expected: The OBU terminates the communication session with the RIU.

test_cases.title: Termination of RIU session when leaving Level 1
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in Level 1 with an active session with an RIU.
test_cases.test_inputs: A transition to a different operational level (e.g., Level 2 or Level 0).

steps.action: The OBU transitions out of Level 1 (e.g., to Level 2).
steps.expected: The OBU terminates the communication session with the RIU.

test_cases.title: OBU acknowledges a received emergency message with its identifier
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, radio session with the supervising RBC is established. The train is in a mode where emergency messages are processed (e.g., FS, OS, LS, AD, SM). No emergency message is currently stored.

steps.action: The RBC sends an emergency message to the OBU containing a specific identification number (NID_EM).
steps.expected: The OBU receives the message and stores it.

steps.action: The OBU processes the received emergency message.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an acknowledgement message (Message 147) to the RBC. The acknowledgement message contains the same identification number (NID_EM) as the received emergency message.

test_cases.title: OBU acknowledges a repeated emergency message with the same identifier
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, radio session with the supervising RBC is established. The OBU has already received and acknowledged an emergency message with identification number NID_EM_1.

steps.action: The RBC sends a new emergency message with the same identification number (NID_EM_1) as the previously received one.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces the previous emergency message with the new one.

steps.action: The OBU processes the new emergency message.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an acknowledgement message to the RBC. The acknowledgement message contains the identification number NID_EM_1.

test_cases.title: Rejection of new MA after accepted conditional emergency stop
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established. Train is in a mode where it can accept a conditional emergency stop (e.g., OS or FS). The train has not yet passed the new stop location indicated in the emergency stop message.
test_cases.test_inputs: Conditional emergency stop message with a valid new stop location. New Movement Authority (MA) message.

steps.action: Send a conditional emergency stop message to the OBU with a new stop location that is ahead of the train's current position.
steps.expected: The OBU accepts the emergency stop message and applies the corresponding supervision (e.g., defines a new EOA/SvL with no release speed).

steps.action: Send a new Movement Authority (MA) message to the OBU while the emergency stop is active and has not been revoked.
steps.expected: The OBU rejects the new Movement Authority. The supervision remains based on the emergency stop, and the new MA is not applied.

test_cases.title: Rejection of new MA after accepted unconditional emergency stop
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established. Train is in a mode where it can accept an unconditional emergency stop (e.g., OS or FS).
test_cases.test_inputs: Unconditional emergency stop message. New Movement Authority (MA) message.

steps.action: Send an unconditional emergency stop message to the OBU.
steps.expected: The OBU accepts the message and trips the train immediately (Emergency Brake).

steps.action: Send a new Movement Authority (MA) message to the OBU while the emergency stop is active and has not been revoked.
steps.expected: The OBU rejects the new Movement Authority. The train remains in the emergency state, and the new MA is not applied.

test_cases.title: Acceptance of new MA after revocation of emergency stop
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established. The OBU has previously accepted an emergency stop message (conditional or unconditional) and is currently in the emergency state.
test_cases.test_inputs: Revocation message for the active emergency stop. New Movement Authority (MA) message.

steps.action: Send a revocation message for the active emergency stop to the OBU.
steps.expected: The OBU revokes the emergency stop. The train supervision returns to the state prior to the emergency stop or a new valid state, and the emergency brake is released if applicable.

steps.action: Send a new Movement Authority (MA) message to the OBU after the revocation.
steps.expected: The OBU accepts the new Movement Authority and applies it to the supervision.

test_cases.title: OBU acknowledges emergency message revocation with correct timestamp
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, mode FS, OS, LS or SM, radio session established with the RBC. An emergency message with a specific identifier has been previously received and acknowledged by the OBU.

steps.action: The RBC sends a revocation message for the previously received emergency message, including the request for acknowledgement and a specific timestamp.
steps.expected: The OBU receives the revocation message.

steps.action: The OBU processes the revocation message.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an acknowledgement message to the RBC.

steps.action: The OBU constructs the acknowledgement message.
steps.expected: The acknowledgement message refers to the timestamp of the revocation message sent by the trackside.

test_cases.title: OBU does not acknowledge inconsistent revocation message
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, mode FS, OS, LS or SM, radio session established with the RBC.
test_cases.assumptions: The revocation message is considered inconsistent if it contains invalid data or fails consistency checks defined in SUBSET-026 §3.16.3.1 and §3.16.3.3.

steps.action: The RBC sends a revocation message for an emergency message that is considered inconsistent (e.g., invalid identifier or corrupted data).
steps.expected: The OBU identifies the message as inconsistent.

steps.action: The OBU processes the inconsistent revocation message.
steps.expected: The OBU does not send an acknowledgement message to the RBC.

test_cases.title: OS mode: Trackside speed limit prevails over National value
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in On-Sight (OS) mode. National value for OS speed limit is set to 30 km/h. A Mode Profile for OS is received from trackside with a speed limit of 20 km/h.

steps.action: Train enters the OS area defined by the Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU applies the trackside speed limit of 20 km/h as the mode-related speed restriction, ignoring the National value of 30 km/h.

test_cases.title: LS mode: Trackside speed limit prevails over National value
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in Limited Supervision (LS) mode. National value for LS speed limit is set to 100 km/h. A Mode Profile for LS is received from trackside with a speed limit of 80 km/h.

steps.action: Train enters the LS area defined by the Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU applies the trackside speed limit of 80 km/h as the mode-related speed restriction, ignoring the National value of 100 km/h.

test_cases.title: SH mode: Trackside speed limit prevails over National value
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in Shunting (SH) mode. National value for SH speed limit is set to 30 km/h. A Mode Profile for SH is received from trackside with a speed limit of 15 km/h.

steps.action: Train enters the SH area defined by the Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU applies the trackside speed limit of 15 km/h as the mode-related speed restriction, ignoring the National value of 30 km/h.

test_cases.title: OS mode: Trackside speed limit higher than National value
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in On-Sight (OS) mode. National value for OS speed limit is set to 30 km/h. A Mode Profile for OS is received from trackside with a speed limit of 40 km/h.

steps.action: Train enters the OS area defined by the Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU applies the trackside speed limit of 40 km/h as the mode-related speed restriction, ignoring the National value of 30 km/h.

test_cases.title: PBD speed restriction calculation upon receipt of trackside data
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where PBD information can be received (Level 1 or 2). No PBD speed restriction is currently active. Trackside is configured to send a valid PBD profile.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid PBD profile containing start/end locations, PBD distance, brake type (Emergency), and gradient.

steps.action: Transmit a valid PBD profile from trackside to the OBU.
steps.expected: The OBU calculates and applies a speed restriction to ensure the permitted braking distance. The calculated speed is visible in the speed profile.

steps.action: Verify the calculated speed restriction value against the expected value derived from the input parameters.
steps.expected: The applied speed restriction matches the expected calculated value.

test_cases.title: PBD speed restriction recalculation upon input change
test_cases.preconditions: OBU has an active PBD speed restriction calculated from a previous PBD profile.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new PBD profile with a different PBD distance or gradient.

steps.action: Transmit a new PBD profile from trackside with a changed PBD distance (e.g., shorter distance).
steps.expected: The OBU recalculates the speed restriction. The new speed restriction value is lower than the previous one, reflecting the shorter braking distance.

steps.action: Verify the new calculated speed restriction value.
steps.expected: The applied speed restriction matches the expected value for the new PBD distance.

test_cases.title: No recalculation when PBD inputs remain unchanged
test_cases.preconditions: OBU has an active PBD speed restriction calculated from a previous PBD profile.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new PBD profile identical to the previous one in all calculation-relevant parameters (PBD distance, gradient, brake type).

steps.action: Transmit a new PBD profile from trackside that is identical to the currently active one in terms of calculation inputs.
steps.expected: The OBU does not recalculate the speed restriction. The speed restriction value remains unchanged.

test_cases.title: PBD calculation with emergency brake and rotating mass compensation
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is configured with specific train data including rotating mass. Trackside sends a PBD profile requiring Emergency Brake.
test_cases.test_inputs: PBD profile with Emergency Brake, specific gradient, and PBD distance. Train data with known rotating mass.
test_cases.assumptions: The expected speed is calculated using the formula in SUBSET-026 §3.11.11.6, including rotating mass compensation for the gradient.

steps.action: Transmit a PBD profile requiring Emergency Brake with a non-zero gradient.
steps.expected: The OBU calculates the PBD speed restriction using the EBD curve. The calculation includes rotating mass compensation for the gradient.

steps.action: Verify the calculated speed restriction against the expected value that includes rotating mass compensation.
steps.expected: The applied speed restriction matches the expected value calculated with rotating mass compensation.

test_cases.title: PBD calculation ignoring adhesion profiles and track conditions
test_cases.preconditions: OBU has stored adhesion profiles and track conditions (brake inhibition, powerless section) that would normally affect deceleration calculations.
test_cases.test_inputs: PBD profile with Emergency Brake. Stored adhesion profiles and track conditions that would reduce deceleration if considered.
test_cases.assumptions: The expected speed is calculated ignoring adhesion profiles and brake-inhibition/powerless-section track conditions, as per SUBSET-026 §3.11.11.4.

steps.action: Transmit a PBD profile requiring Emergency Brake.
steps.expected: The OBU calculates the PBD speed restriction. The calculation ignores the stored adhesion profiles and brake-inhibition/powerless-section track conditions.

steps.action: Verify the calculated speed restriction against the expected value that ignores these factors.
steps.expected: The applied speed restriction matches the expected value calculated without considering adhesion profiles and specific track conditions.

test_cases.title: PBD calculation with service brake and SBD curve
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is configured with specific train data. Trackside sends a PBD profile requiring Service Brake.
test_cases.test_inputs: PBD profile with Service Brake, specific gradient, and PBD distance.
test_cases.assumptions: The expected speed is calculated using the SBD curve, as per SUBSET-026 §3.11.11.9.

steps.action: Transmit a PBD profile requiring Service Brake.
steps.expected: The OBU calculates the PBD speed restriction using the SBD curve. The calculation includes the expected deceleration and reaches zero speed at the PBD distance.

steps.action: Verify the calculated speed restriction against the expected value derived from the SBD curve.
steps.expected: The applied speed restriction matches the expected value calculated using the SBD curve.

test_cases.title: PBD speed restriction calculation with emergency brake
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where PBD information can be received. Trackside sends a PBD profile requiring Emergency Brake.
test_cases.test_inputs: PBD profile with Emergency Brake, specific gradient, and PBD distance.
test_cases.assumptions: The expected speed is calculated using the EBD-based inequalities in SUBSET-026 §3.11.11.6.

steps.action: Transmit a PBD profile requiring Emergency Brake.
steps.expected: The OBU calculates the PBD speed restriction as the speed satisfying the EBD-based inequalities, rounded down as specified.

steps.action: Verify the calculated speed restriction against the expected value.
steps.expected: The applied speed restriction matches the expected value calculated from the EBD-based inequalities.

test_cases.title: PBD speed restriction set to zero if no speed satisfies inequalities
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where PBD information can be received. Trackside sends a PBD profile with a very short PBD distance or high gradient that makes it impossible to satisfy the EBD-based inequalities with any positive speed.
test_cases.test_inputs: PBD profile with Emergency Brake, very short PBD distance or high gradient.
test_cases.assumptions: The expected speed is zero, as no positive speed satisfies the EBD-based inequalities.

steps.action: Transmit a PBD profile with a very short PBD distance or high gradient.
steps.expected: The OBU calculates the PBD speed restriction as zero, as no positive speed satisfies the EBD-based inequalities.

steps.action: Verify the calculated speed restriction.
steps.expected: The applied speed restriction is zero.

test_cases.title: Tunnel stopping area start indication uses estimated front end
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 or 2, mode FS. A tunnel stopping area is stored on-board with a known start location (Point D). The train is moving towards the tunnel stopping area. The estimated front end position is known.

steps.action: The train moves such that the estimated front end reaches the calculated announcement point (Point C), which is in rear of the tunnel stopping area start (Point D).
steps.expected: The DMI displays the 'Tunnel Stopping Area announcement' indication.

steps.action: The train continues to move until the estimated front end reaches the start location of the tunnel stopping area (Point D).
steps.expected: The DMI updates the indication to 'Tunnel Stopping Area' (or similar active indication) and the remaining distance to the start location is no longer displayed as a future distance.

test_cases.title: Sound horn indication start uses estimated front end
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 or 2, mode FS. A 'Sound horn' track condition is stored on-board with a known start location (Point D). The train is moving towards the sound horn area. The estimated front end position is known.

steps.action: The train moves such that the estimated front end reaches the calculated display point (Point C), which is in rear of the sound horn area start (Point D).
steps.expected: The DMI displays the 'Sound horn' indication.

test_cases.title: Sound horn indication end uses estimated front end
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 or 2, mode FS. The 'Sound horn' indication is currently displayed on the DMI. The train is moving through the sound horn area. The end location of the sound horn area (Point E) is known.

steps.action: The train moves such that the estimated front end reaches the end location of the sound horn area (Point E).
steps.expected: The DMI removes the 'Sound horn' indication.

test_cases.title: Tunnel stopping area evaluation with high speed (boundary)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 or 2, mode FS. A tunnel stopping area is stored. The train is moving at a high speed where the distance between the estimated front end and the max safe front end is significant.

steps.action: The train moves such that the max safe front end passes the start of the tunnel stopping area (Point D), but the estimated front end is still in rear of Point D.
steps.expected: The DMI does NOT display the active 'Tunnel Stopping Area' indication yet, because the evaluation is based on the estimated front end, not the max safe front end.

steps.action: The train continues to move until the estimated front end reaches Point D.
steps.expected: The DMI displays the active 'Tunnel Stopping Area' indication.

test_cases.title: Route suitability unsuitability due to loading gauge mismatch
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where route suitability data can be received (e.g., Level 1 or 2). Valid Train Data is stored on-board with a specific loading gauge profile. The train is moving or ready to move.
test_cases.test_inputs: Route suitability data from trackside containing a list of accepted loading gauges that does NOT include the train's stored loading gauge profile. Traction system and axle load category in the data are compatible with the train.

steps.action: Transmit route suitability data from trackside to the OBU where the list of accepted loading gauges excludes the train's current loading gauge profile.
steps.expected: The OBU compares the data with stored Train Data and identifies a loading gauge unsuitability.

steps.action: Observe the OBU's response regarding the unsuitability.
steps.expected: The OBU considers the unsuitability to exist and informs the driver about the loading gauge unsuitability.

test_cases.title: Route suitability unsuitability due to axle load category mismatch
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where route suitability data can be received. Valid Train Data is stored on-board with a specific axle load category. The train is moving or ready to move.
test_cases.test_inputs: Route suitability data from trackside containing a list of permitted axle load categories that does NOT include the train's stored axle load category. Loading gauge and traction system in the data are compatible with the train.

steps.action: Transmit route suitability data from trackside to the OBU where the list of permitted axle load categories excludes the train's current axle load category.
steps.expected: The OBU compares the data with stored Train Data and identifies an axle load category unsuitability.

steps.action: Observe the OBU's response regarding the unsuitability.
steps.expected: The OBU considers the unsuitability to exist and informs the driver about the axle load category unsuitability.

test_cases.title: Route suitability unsuitability due to traction system mismatch
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where route suitability data can be received. Valid Train Data is stored on-board. The engine is NOT capable of running on a line without any traction system (i.e., it requires a specific traction system).
test_cases.test_inputs: Route suitability data from trackside containing a traction system that is NOT among those accepted by the engine. Loading gauge and axle load category in the data are compatible with the train.

steps.action: Transmit route suitability data from trackside to the OBU specifying a traction system that the engine does not accept.
steps.expected: The OBU compares the data with stored Train Data and identifies a traction system unsuitability.

steps.action: Observe the OBU's response regarding the unsuitability.
steps.expected: The OBU considers the unsuitability to exist and informs the driver about the traction system unsuitability.

test_cases.title: No route suitability unsuitability when all parameters match
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where route suitability data can be received. Valid Train Data is stored on-board.
test_cases.test_inputs: Route suitability data from trackside where the train's loading gauge is in the accepted list, the train's axle load category is in the permitted list, and the traction system is accepted by the engine.

steps.action: Transmit route suitability data from trackside to the OBU where all parameters (loading gauge, axle load category, traction system) are compatible with the stored Train Data.
steps.expected: The OBU compares the data with stored Train Data and finds no unsuitability.

steps.action: Observe the OBU's status regarding route suitability.
steps.expected: The OBU does not report any unsuitability to the driver and allows the train to proceed without route suitability restrictions.

test_cases.title: No traction system unsuitability for engine capable of running without traction system
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where route suitability data can be received. Valid Train Data is stored on-board. The engine IS capable of running on a line without any traction system.
test_cases.test_inputs: Route suitability data from trackside specifying a traction system that is NOT among those accepted by the engine (or no traction system specified, depending on interpretation, but specifically a mismatch scenario). Loading gauge and axle load category are compatible.

steps.action: Transmit route suitability data from trackside to the OBU specifying a traction system that does not match the engine's accepted list, but the engine is configured/capable to run on a line without any traction system.
steps.expected: The OBU compares the data with stored Train Data.

steps.action: Observe the OBU's evaluation of the traction system parameter.
steps.expected: The OBU does NOT find a traction system unsuitability, despite the mismatch, because the engine can run on a line without any traction system.

test_cases.title: Train runs without route suitability data and no default values are supervised
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a level where route suitability data could be received. No route suitability data has been received from trackside. The OBU is in its initial state regarding route suitability.
test_cases.test_inputs: No route suitability data transmitted from trackside.

steps.action: Operate the train without receiving any route suitability data from trackside.
steps.expected: The OBU allows the train to run.

steps.action: Check the OBU's internal state and supervision logic for route suitability.
steps.expected: The OBU does not use any default route suitability values and does not supervise any route suitability restrictions. The state is 'no route suitability restriction exists'.

test_cases.title: Text message appearance for auxiliary information without acknowledgement
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed (e.g., FS or OS). No text message is currently displayed.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with class 'auxiliary information' and 'driver acknowledgement not requested'.

steps.action: Receive a text message from trackside with class 'auxiliary information' and no driver acknowledgement request.
steps.expected: The OBU displays the text message with the appearance defined for auxiliary information without acknowledgement (e.g., specific color, font, or position as per HMI specification).

test_cases.title: Text message appearance for important information with acknowledgement
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed. No text message is currently displayed.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with class 'important information' and 'driver acknowledgement requested'.

steps.action: Receive a text message from trackside with class 'important information' and driver acknowledgement requested.
steps.expected: The OBU displays the text message with the appearance defined for important information with acknowledgement (e.g., distinct from auxiliary, possibly with a prompt to acknowledge).

test_cases.title: Start condition with multiple sub-conditions defined as 'any'
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed. Train is moving.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with start condition defined by two sub-conditions (e.g., 'location' and 'speed') with the logic 'any' (OR). The train is not at the location but is at the speed.

steps.action: Receive a text message where the start condition requires either 'location A' OR 'speed > 50 km/h'. The train is at speed 60 km/h but not at location A.
steps.expected: The OBU considers the start condition fulfilled because one of the sub-conditions (speed) is met, and the text message is displayed.

test_cases.title: Start condition with no sub-conditions defined
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with no start sub-conditions defined.

steps.action: Receive a text message from trackside that does not define any start sub-conditions.
steps.expected: The OBU treats the start condition as immediately fulfilled and displays the text message (provided the end condition is not also immediately fulfilled).

test_cases.title: Driver acknowledgement ends display regardless of end condition
test_cases.preconditions: A text message requesting driver acknowledgement is displayed. The end condition is defined as 'location B' which has not been reached. The message is configured such that acknowledgement always ends the display.

steps.action: The driver acknowledges the text message before reaching location B.
steps.expected: The text message display ends immediately upon acknowledgement, even though the end condition (location B) has not been fulfilled.

test_cases.title: Driver acknowledgement is a necessary condition for ending display
test_cases.preconditions: A text message requesting driver acknowledgement is displayed. The end condition is defined as 'location B'. The message is configured such that acknowledgement is a necessary condition in addition to the end condition.

steps.action: The train reaches location B (end condition fulfilled) but the driver has not acknowledged the message.
steps.expected: The text message remains displayed because the driver acknowledgement is a necessary condition that has not been met.

steps.action: The driver acknowledges the text message after reaching location B.
steps.expected: The text message display ends because both the end condition and the driver acknowledgement are now fulfilled.

test_cases.title: No display if end condition is immediately fulfilled
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with start condition 'immediately fulfilled' (no sub-conditions) and end condition 'location A' where the train is currently at location A.

steps.action: Receive a text message where the start condition is immediately fulfilled and the end condition (location A) is also already fulfilled at the moment of receipt.
steps.expected: The OBU does not display the text message at all, even if driver confirmation is requested.

test_cases.title: Display length measured from start location
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed. Train is moving.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with start condition 'location A' and end condition 'location B' where the length between A and B is 1000m. The train is at location A.

steps.action: The train passes location A (start condition fulfilled).
steps.expected: The text message is displayed.

steps.action: The train travels 500m from location A.
steps.expected: The text message is still displayed.

steps.action: The train travels another 500m, reaching location B (1000m from A).
steps.expected: The text message display ends because the end condition (location B) is fulfilled, and the length was measured from the start location A.

test_cases.title: Driver acknowledgement report sent to RBC
test_cases.preconditions: A communication session with an RBC is established. A text message requesting a report of driver acknowledgement is displayed.

steps.action: The driver acknowledges the text message.
steps.expected: The OBU sends a driver acknowledgement report to the RBC referenced in the request, including the text message identifier.

test_cases.title: Rejection of duplicate text message identifier
test_cases.preconditions: A text message with identifier 'ID-123' requesting a report of driver acknowledgement has been received and is currently displayed, not yet acknowledged by the driver.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new text message with the same identifier 'ID-123' requesting a report of driver acknowledgement.

steps.action: Receive a new text message from trackside with identifier 'ID-123' requesting a report of driver acknowledgement.
steps.expected: The OBU rejects the new text message and does not display it, because it has the same identifier as a previously received message that has not yet been acknowledged.

test_cases.title: Infill MA with OS/LS Mode Profile: Deletion beyond reference location
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. A valid MA with an OS Mode Profile is stored and being supervised. The train is moving towards the Mode Profile start location.
test_cases.test_inputs: Infill MA containing a new OS Mode Profile. Infill reference location is defined.
test_cases.assumptions: The infill reference location is within the range of the currently supervised OS Mode Profile.

steps.action: Receive an infill MA that includes a new OS Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU processes the infill MA.

steps.action: Check the status of the previously supervised OS Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The previously supervised OS Mode Profile is deleted only beyond the infill reference location. The part of the profile before the infill reference location remains valid/supervised.

test_cases.title: Infill MA with SH Mode Profile: Infill reference at or rear of SH start
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. A valid MA with a SH Mode Profile is stored and being supervised. The train is moving towards the SH Mode Profile start location.
test_cases.test_inputs: Infill MA. Infill reference location is at or in rear of the start location of the currently supervised SH Mode Profile.

steps.action: Receive an infill MA where the infill reference location is at or in rear of the start location of the currently supervised SH Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU processes the infill MA.

steps.action: Check the status of the previously supervised SH Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The currently supervised SH Mode Profile is deleted.

test_cases.title: Infill MA with SH Mode Profile: Infill reference in advance of SH start
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. A valid MA with a SH Mode Profile is stored and being supervised. The train is moving towards the SH Mode Profile start location.
test_cases.test_inputs: Infill MA containing a new Mode Profile and a list of balise groups for SH area. Infill reference location is in advance of the start location of the currently supervised SH Mode Profile.

steps.action: Receive an infill MA where the infill reference location is in advance of the start location of the currently supervised SH Mode Profile. The infill MA contains a new Mode Profile and a list of balise groups for SH area.
steps.expected: The OBU processes the infill MA.

steps.action: Check the status of the previously supervised SH Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The currently supervised SH Mode Profile is NOT deleted. It remains active.

steps.action: Check the handling of the new Mode Profile and SH balise group list in the infill MA.
steps.expected: The new Mode Profile and the list of balise groups for SH area included in the infill MA are ignored by the OBU.

test_cases.title: Temporary EOA and SvL: Mode Profile requires SvL at start
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. A new MA with a Mode Profile (e.g., OS or LS) is received. The Mode Profile requires a temporary SvL at its start location. The OBU has not yet switched to the Mode Profile's mode.
test_cases.test_inputs: MA with Mode Profile requiring SvL at start.

steps.action: Receive a new MA with a Mode Profile that requires a temporary SvL at the Mode Profile start location.
steps.expected: The OBU treats the Mode Profile start location as a temporary EOA.

steps.action: Check the Supervised Location (SvL) definition.
steps.expected: The OBU considers a temporary SvL without release speed at the Mode Profile start location.

test_cases.title: Temporary EOA and SvL: No SvL required, MA has LOA at/beyond profile start
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. A new MA with a Mode Profile is received. The Mode Profile does NOT require a temporary SvL. The MA defines an LOA located in advance of or at the start of the Mode Profile. The OBU has not yet switched to the Mode Profile's mode.
test_cases.test_inputs: MA with Mode Profile (no SvL required) and LOA at or beyond Mode Profile start.
test_cases.assumptions: The calculation of the SvL as per SUBSET-026 §3.8.4.5 (as if no LOA were given) results in a specific location.

steps.action: Receive a new MA with a Mode Profile that does not require a temporary SvL, where the MA has an LOA located in advance of or at the start of the Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU treats the Mode Profile start location as a temporary EOA.

steps.action: Check the Supervised Location (SvL) definition.
steps.expected: The OBU considers a temporary SvL without release speed at the location determined in accordance with SUBSET-026 §3.8.4.5 as if no LOA had been given.

test_cases.title: Temporary EOA and SvL: No SvL required, MA has LOA in rear of profile start
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. A new MA with a Mode Profile is received. The Mode Profile does NOT require a temporary SvL. The MA defines an LOA located in rear of the start of the Mode Profile. The OBU has not yet switched to the Mode Profile's mode.
test_cases.test_inputs: MA with Mode Profile (no SvL required) and LOA in rear of Mode Profile start.

steps.action: Receive a new MA with a Mode Profile that does not require a temporary SvL, where the MA has an LOA located in rear of the start of the Mode Profile.
steps.expected: The OBU treats the Mode Profile start location as a temporary EOA.

steps.action: Check the Supervised Location (SvL) definition.
steps.expected: The OBU considers a temporary SvL without release speed at the Mode Profile start location.

test_cases.title: Replacement of Level Crossing information with identical identity
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where Level Crossing information is processed (e.g., FS, OS, LS, AD, or SM). A Level Crossing (LX) information set with Identity ID_A is already stored in the OBU memory. The train has not yet passed the start location of the stored LX.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new Level Crossing information message with Identity ID_A, but with different parameters (e.g., different length, different protection status, or different start location) than the currently stored one.

steps.action: Verify that the OBU currently holds LX information with Identity ID_A and note its parameters (e.g., start location, length, protection status).
steps.expected: The OBU displays or logs the stored LX information with Identity ID_A and its original parameters.

steps.action: Transmit a new Level Crossing information message to the OBU with the same Identity ID_A but with modified parameters (e.g., a different length or protection status).
steps.expected: The OBU accepts the new information and replaces the previously stored LX information with Identity ID_A. The old parameters are no longer active.

steps.action: Check the active Level Crossing information in the OBU (via HMI or diagnostic interface).
steps.expected: The OBU displays the new parameters associated with Identity ID_A. The old parameters are not present.

test_cases.title: Independence of Level Crossing information with different identities
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where Level Crossing information is processed. Two distinct Level Crossing information sets, LX_1 with Identity ID_A and LX_2 with Identity ID_B, are stored in the OBU memory.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new Level Crossing information message with Identity ID_A and modified parameters.

steps.action: Verify that both LX_1 (Identity ID_A) and LX_2 (Identity ID_B) are stored and active in the OBU.
steps.expected: The OBU holds both Level Crossing information sets independently.

steps.action: Transmit a new Level Crossing information message with Identity ID_A and modified parameters.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces the stored information for Identity ID_A with the new data.

steps.action: Check the status of the Level Crossing information with Identity ID_B.
steps.expected: The Level Crossing information with Identity ID_B remains unchanged and active, confirming that the update to ID_A did not affect ID_B.

test_cases.title: Phishing-resistant authentication option is available and functional at AAL2
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account exists with a phishing-resistant authenticator (e.g., passkey or FIDO2 security key) bound to it.

steps.action: Navigate to the VBP sign-in page for company representatives.
steps.expected: The sign-in interface presents at least one phishing-resistant authentication option (e.g., 'Sign in with Passkey' or 'Use Security Key') alongside other AAL2 options.

steps.action: Select the phishing-resistant authentication option and complete the authentication using the bound authenticator.
steps.expected: Authentication completes successfully, and the user is granted access to the company representative account.

test_cases.title: Phishing-resistant authentication prevents credential disclosure to impostor verifier
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a phishing-resistant authenticator (e.g., passkey) is available. A test environment simulating an impostor verifier (phishing site) is set up.
test_cases.assumptions: The phishing-resistant authenticator is configured to be bound to the legitimate VBP domain only.

steps.action: Attempt to authenticate using the phishing-resistant authenticator on the impostor verifier site (phishing page) that mimics the VBP sign-in interface.
steps.expected: The authenticator refuses to provide credentials or authentication output to the impostor verifier because the domain does not match the registered origin.

steps.action: Verify that no valid authentication token or secret is disclosed to the impostor verifier during the failed attempt.
steps.expected: The impostor verifier receives no valid authentication data, and the user's account remains secure.

test_cases.title: Authentication with a multi-factor authenticator (passkey with biometric)
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is active at AAL2 with a multi-factor authenticator (e.g., a passkey requiring biometric activation) bound.

steps.action: Initiate sign-in for the company representative account and select the bound multi-factor authenticator.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the activation factor (e.g., biometric scan) associated with the multi-factor authenticator.

steps.action: Provide the required activation factor to complete the authentication event.
steps.expected: Authentication succeeds and the user is granted access to the portal at AAL2.

test_cases.title: Authentication with a combination of two separate factors (password + TOTP)
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is active at AAL2 with a password (knowledge factor) and a TOTP app (possession factor) bound.

steps.action: Enter the correct password for the company representative account.
steps.expected: The system accepts the first factor and prompts for the second factor (TOTP code).

steps.action: Enter the current valid TOTP code from the bound authenticator app.
steps.expected: Authentication succeeds and the user is granted access to the portal at AAL2.

test_cases.title: Authentication with only one factor is rejected
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is active at AAL2 with a password and a TOTP app bound.

steps.action: Enter the correct password for the company representative account.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second factor.

steps.action: Attempt to bypass the second factor step or submit an empty/invalid second factor.
steps.expected: Authentication fails and access to the account is denied.

test_cases.title: Inactivity timeout terminates AAL2 session
