steps.action: As a company representative, bind a second authenticator (e.g., a passkey) to the account.
steps.expected: The binding is successful and the account now has two bound authenticators.

steps.action: As a company representative, bind a third authenticator (e.g., a second TOTP app) to the account.
steps.expected: The binding is successful and the account now has three bound authenticators.

steps.action: View the list of bound authenticators in the account settings.
steps.expected: All three authenticators (the original TOTP app, the passkey, and the second TOTP app) are listed as active.

test_cases.title: Binding an AAL2 authenticator to an AAL2 account requires AAL2 authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a maximum available AAL of AAL2 (password + TOTP bound). A new AAL2-capable authenticator (e.g., passkey) is ready to be bound.

steps.action: Initiate the binding of the new AAL2 authenticator while authenticated at AAL1 (password only, if the system allows partial sessions for management) or attempt to bind without completing the second factor.
steps.expected: The system rejects the binding request or prompts for the second factor, as the required authentication level is AAL2 (lower of AAL2 account max and AAL2 authenticator max).

steps.action: Complete the full AAL2 authentication (password + TOTP) and then initiate the binding of the new AAL2 authenticator.
steps.expected: The binding process is allowed to proceed.

test_cases.title: Binding an AAL1 authenticator to an AAL2 account requires AAL1 authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a maximum available AAL of AAL2 (password + TOTP bound). A new AAL1-capable authenticator (e.g., SMS OTP) is ready to be bound.
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports binding AAL1 authenticators to AAL2 accounts for recovery or alternative access.

steps.action: Initiate the binding of the new AAL1 authenticator while authenticated at AAL1 (password only).
steps.expected: The binding process is allowed to proceed, as the required authentication level is AAL1 (lower of AAL2 account max and AAL1 authenticator max).

test_cases.title: Binding an AAL3 authenticator to an AAL2 account requires AAL2 authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a maximum available AAL of AAL2 (password + TOTP bound). A new AAL3-capable authenticator (e.g., FIDO2 with strong biometrics) is ready to be bound.
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports binding AAL3 authenticators to AAL2 accounts.

steps.action: Initiate the binding of the new AAL3 authenticator while authenticated at AAL1 (password only).
steps.expected: The system rejects the binding request or prompts for the second factor, as the required authentication level is AAL2 (lower of AAL2 account max and AAL3 authenticator max).

steps.action: Complete the full AAL2 authentication (password + TOTP) and then initiate the binding of the new AAL3 authenticator.
steps.expected: The binding process is allowed to proceed.

test_cases.title: Notification sent via independent channel upon authenticator binding
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a registered email address and a valid second-factor authenticator (e.g., TOTP) bound. The representative is authenticated at AAL2.
test_cases.assumptions: The 'independent mechanism' is implemented as an email notification to the registered address, distinct from the in-app session or the binding transaction channel.

steps.action: Initiate the binding of a new authenticator (e.g., a new passkey or TOTP app) to the account.
steps.expected: The binding process starts and prompts for the new authenticator's credentials or code.

steps.action: Complete the binding process successfully.
steps.expected: The new authenticator is added to the account.

steps.action: Check the registered email inbox of the company representative.
steps.expected: A notification email is received informing the representative that a new authenticator has been added to their account.

test_cases.title: Notification is not sent if authenticator binding fails
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a registered email address. The representative is authenticated at AAL2.
test_cases.assumptions: The binding process can be intentionally failed by providing an invalid code or cancelling the process.

steps.action: Initiate the binding of a new authenticator.
steps.expected: The binding process starts.

steps.action: Provide an invalid code or cancel the binding process so that the binding fails.
steps.expected: The binding is not completed, and an error message is displayed.

steps.action: Check the registered email inbox of the company representative.
steps.expected: No notification email regarding a new authenticator addition is received.

test_cases.title: E-posta onay kodunun başarılı kullanımdan sonra geçersiz kılınması

test_cases.title: Merkezi kayıt yönetim sistemine aktarım hatasında otomatik uyarı gönderimi
test_cases.preconditions: Portal ve arka ofis bileşenleri çalışmaktadır. Merkezi kayıt yönetim sistemi (Log Management System) ile portal arasındaki bağlantı test edilebilir durumda olup, aktarım hatası simüle edilebilmektedir. SOME ve nöbetçi yönetici uyarı kanalları (e-posta/SMS) test ortamında izlenebilir durumdadır.
test_cases.test_inputs: Kayıt aktarım hatası simülasyonu (örneğin merkezi sisteme ağ kesintisi veya yetki hatası verilmesi).
test_cases.assumptions: Uyarı mekanizmasının 15 dakika içinde tetiklenmesi için sistem saati hızlandırılabilir veya uyarı zamanlayıcısı test amaçlı ayarlanabilir.

steps.action: Portal veya arka ofis bileşenlerinden merkezi kayıt yönetim sistemine log aktarımı sırasında bir hata (örneğin bağlantı kesintisi) oluşturulur.
steps.expected: Sistem, hata oluştuğunu algılar ve uyarı tetikleyicisini başlatır.

steps.action: Uyarı tetiklenmesinden itibaren 15 dakika beklenir (veya test ortamında süre hızlandırılır).
steps.expected: KHGM SOME ekibi ve nöbetçi yöneticiye otomatik olarak uyarı mesajı gönderilir.

steps.action: Gönderilen uyarıların içeriği ve zamanlaması kontrol edilir.
steps.expected: Uyarılar, hata detaylarını içerecek şekilde ve 15 dakikalık süre zarfında (veya testte hızlandırılmış eşdeğer sürede) iletildiği doğrulanır.

test_cases.title: Merkezi kayıt yönetim sisteminde logların toplanması ve yetkili personel erişimi
test_cases.preconditions: Portal ve arka ofis bileşenleri aktif olarak log üretmektedir. Merkezi kayıt yönetim sistemi yapılandırılmıştır. Yetkili personel hesabı mevcuttur.
test_cases.test_inputs: Portal ve arka ofisten üretilen örnek log kayıtları (ayrıcalıklı işlem ve genel güvenlik kayıtları).

steps.action: Portal ve arka ofis bileşenlerinde çeşitli işlemler (giriş, yetkili işlem, hata) gerçekleştirilerek loglar üretilir.
steps.expected: Loglar, uygulamadan ayrı merkezi kayıt yönetim sistemine başarıyla aktarılır.

steps.action: Yetkili personel hesabıyla merkezi kayıt yönetim sistemine giriş yapılır ve loglar görüntülenir.
steps.expected: Üretilen loglar merkezi sistemde görüntülenebilir durumda olur ve yetkili personel tarafından erişilebilir.

steps.action: Ayrıcalıklı işlemlere ait logların her iş günü, genel güvenlik kayıtlarının haftalık olarak gözden geçirilebilir yapıda olduğu kontrol edilir.
steps.expected: Loglar, belirlenen periyotlarda (günlük/haftalık) analiz ve inceleme için uygun formatta ve erişilebilirlikte merkezi sistemde tutulmaktadır.

test_cases.title: Geçerli e-Devlet imzası ile oturum açma
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet test ortamına entegre edilmiştir. e-Devlet test IdP'si, VBP'nin doğrulama anahtarına sahip geçerli imzalı assertion'lar üretebilmektedir. Test vatandaş kimliği mevcuttur.

steps.action: Vatandaş olarak e-Devlet üzerinden giriş başlatılır ve e-Devlet tarafından VBP'ye gönderilen assertion'ın imzası, e-Devlet'e ait doğrulama anahtarıyla doğrulanabilir şekilde imzalanmış olduğundan emin olunur.
steps.expected: VBP assertion'ı kabul eder ve vatandaş oturumu açılır.

test_cases.title: Geçersiz imzalı assertion'ın reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet test ortamına entegre edilmiştir. VBP'nin federation endpoint'ine doğrudan assertion gönderilebilecek bir araç (örneğin intercepting proxy veya test istemcisi) mevcuttur.
test_cases.assumptions: Assertion içeriği (issuer, audience, nonce vb.) geçerli olsa da imzanın doğrulanamaz olduğu varsayılır.

steps.action: e-Devlet'e ait doğrulama anahtarıyla doğrulanamayan (örneğin farklı bir anahtarla imzalanmış veya bozulmuş) bir assertion, VBP'nin federation endpoint'ine gönderilir.
steps.expected: VBP assertion'ı reddeder ve oturum açılmaz.

test_cases.title: Beklenmeyen IdP'den gelen assertion'ın reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet test ortamına entegre edilmiştir. VBP'nin federation endpoint'ine doğrudan assertion gönderilebilecek bir araç mevcuttur. VBP'nin güvenmediği veya beklenmeyen bir IdP'nin doğrulama anahtarına sahip bir test ortamı mevcuttur.
test_cases.assumptions: Assertion'ın issuer alanı e-Devlet'i gösterse de, imzanın beklenmeyen bir IdP'nin anahtarıyla atıldığı varsayılır.

steps.action: Issuer alanı e-Devlet'i gösteren ancak imzası beklenmeyen bir IdP'nin doğrulama anahtarıyla doğrulanamayan bir assertion, VBP'nin federation endpoint'ine gönderilir.
steps.expected: VBP assertion'ı reddeder ve oturum açılmaz.

test_cases.title: Acceptance of a valid e-Devlet assertion on first presentation
test_cases.preconditions: A test e-Devlet IdP or test double is configured to issue valid assertions for VBP. A test citizen identity is available. An intercepting proxy or test harness is available to capture and replay assertions.

steps.action: Initiate a sign-in flow as a test citizen through the e-Devlet test IdP.
steps.expected: The e-Devlet IdP issues a valid assertion and redirects to VBP's callback URL.

steps.action: Allow VBP to process the assertion for the first time.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the assertion, validates it, and establishes a citizen session.

test_cases.title: Rejection of a replayed e-Devlet assertion
test_cases.preconditions: A valid e-Devlet assertion has already been successfully processed by VBP to establish a session. The same assertion is captured and available for replay.

steps.action: Present the exact same e-Devlet assertion that was previously accepted to VBP's callback endpoint again.
steps.expected: VBP rejects the assertion due to replay protection and does not establish a new session or extend the existing one.

steps.action: Verify the system logs or error response for the rejected request.
steps.expected: The rejection is logged or indicated as a replay attack or invalid assertion state.

test_cases.title: VBP initiates the federation transaction as the RP
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured with a valid e-Devlet test IdP endpoint. A test citizen account exists in the e-Devlet test environment. An intercepting proxy or browser developer tools are available to capture network traffic.

steps.action: Initiate a citizen login on the VBP portal.
steps.expected: VBP generates an authorization request and redirects the user's browser to the e-Devlet IdP endpoint. The request is initiated by VBP (the RP), not by the IdP.

steps.action: Inspect the captured authorization request sent to e-Devlet.
steps.expected: The request contains VBP's client identifier (RP identifier) and a cryptographic nonce, confirming VBP initiated the transaction as specified in NIST SP 800-63C-4 §2.3.

test_cases.title: Unsuccessful applicant receives generic error for mismatched self-asserted data
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant account is created with self-asserted information that does not match the authoritative source (e.g., incorrect date of birth or national ID number).
test_cases.test_inputs: Applicant credentials and self-asserted data with a known mismatch.

steps.action: Submit the proofing and enrolment form with the self-asserted information that is known to be incorrect.
steps.expected: The system rejects the application and displays a generic error message indicating that the information could not be verified, without specifying which field is incorrect or that it does not match the authoritative source.

steps.action: Submit the proofing and enrolment form again with the same incorrect self-asserted information.
steps.expected: The system rejects the application with the same generic error message, providing no additional details or hints about the specific mismatch.

test_cases.title: Unsuccessful applicant receives generic error for missing self-asserted data
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant account is created. The authoritative source has complete records for the applicant.
test_cases.test_inputs: Applicant credentials and self-asserted data with a missing critical field (e.g., empty national ID number).

steps.action: Submit the proofing and enrolment form with a critical self-asserted field left empty.
steps.expected: The system rejects the application and displays a generic error message indicating that the information could not be verified, without explicitly stating that the field was missing or that it does not match the authoritative source.

test_cases.title: Successful applicant receives distinct success message
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant account is created with self-asserted information that exactly matches the authoritative source.
test_cases.test_inputs: Applicant credentials and correct self-asserted data.

steps.action: Submit the proofing and enrolment form with the correct self-asserted information.
steps.expected: The system accepts the application and displays a success message confirming that the identity proofing was successful.

test_cases.title: Validation of core attributes against an authoritative source
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with valid core attributes (government identifier, name, date of birth) that exist in the authoritative source (e.g., e-Devlet or Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri test database).
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid government identifier and core attributes matching the authoritative source.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing for a company representative and provide valid core attributes that match the authoritative source.
steps.expected: The system validates the attributes against the authoritative source and confirms their accuracy.

steps.action: Complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is successful, and the account is created or updated with the validated attributes.

test_cases.title: Validation of digitally signed attributes on SUPERIOR evidence
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with a valid SUPERIOR evidence document (e.g., digital ID card) containing digitally signed core attributes and a valid issuer public key available in the system's trust store.
test_cases.test_inputs: SUPERIOR evidence with valid digital signatures on core attributes.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing for a company representative and present SUPERIOR evidence with digitally signed core attributes.
steps.expected: The system validates the digital signatures using the issuer's public key and confirms the accuracy of the attributes.

steps.action: Complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is successful, and the account is created or updated with the validated attributes.

test_cases.title: Rejection of attributes that do not match the authoritative source
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with core attributes that do not match the authoritative source (e.g., incorrect date of birth or name).
test_cases.test_inputs: Core attributes with one field (e.g., date of birth) differing from the authoritative source.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing for a company representative and provide core attributes where one field does not match the authoritative source.
steps.expected: The system fails to validate the attributes against the authoritative source.

steps.action: Attempt to complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is rejected, and an error message indicating attribute mismatch is displayed.

test_cases.title: Rejection of SUPERIOR evidence with invalid digital signatures
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with SUPERIOR evidence containing digitally signed core attributes where the signature is invalid or the issuer's public key is not trusted.
test_cases.test_inputs: SUPERIOR evidence with an invalid or untrusted digital signature on core attributes.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing for a company representative and present SUPERIOR evidence with an invalid digital signature.
steps.expected: The system fails to validate the digital signatures using the issuer's public key.

steps.action: Attempt to complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is rejected, and an error message indicating invalid evidence or signature is displayed.

test_cases.title: Notification of proofing sent to validated address with required content
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in the state immediately after successful IAL2 identity proofing. A validated postal address or phone number is associated with the applicant.
test_cases.assumptions: The notification channel (email, SMS, or postal mail) is monitored in the test environment to capture the message content.

steps.action: Complete the IAL2 identity proofing process for a company representative with a validated address.
steps.expected: The system triggers the sending of a notification of proofing to the validated address.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the received notification.
steps.expected: The notification includes the name of the identity service and the date on which the identity proofing was completed.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the received notification for dispute instructions.
steps.expected: The notification provides clear instructions, including contact information, on actions for the recipient to take if they repudiate their participation in the identity proofing event.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the received notification for security and confidentiality information.
steps.expected: The notification provides information about how the organization or CSP protects the security and confidentiality of the information it collects.

steps.action: Inspect the content of the received notification for subscriber responsibilities.
steps.expected: The notification provides information about any responsibilities that the recipient has as a subscriber of the identity service.

test_cases.title: Notification not sent if proofing is unsuccessful
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative is attempting IAL2 identity proofing with invalid or mismatched evidence.

steps.action: Attempt IAL2 identity proofing for a company representative using evidence that fails validation (e.g., mismatched government identifier).
steps.expected: The identity proofing process fails and is not completed successfully.

steps.action: Check the validated address of the applicant for any notification of proofing.
steps.expected: No notification of proofing is sent to the validated address.

test_cases.title: Knowledge-based verification is not used during company representative proofing
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with a company representative proofing flow accessible. The flow is configured to allow identity verification steps.

steps.action: Initiate the company representative proofing flow and proceed to the identity verification step.
steps.expected: The system does not present any knowledge-based verification questions (e.g., 'What was your first pet's name?', 'What is your mother's maiden name?') as a method to verify identity.

steps.action: Complete the identity verification using the approved non-KBV methods (e.g., document verification, biometric comparison, or out-of-band code) and observe the available options throughout the process.
steps.expected: At no point during the identity verification phase is the user prompted to answer personal knowledge questions to prove their identity.

test_cases.title: Email is not offered as an out-of-band authentication method
test_cases.preconditions: A registered user account with the ability to configure or select authentication methods for out-of-band verification.

steps.action: Navigate to the security or authentication settings page for the user account.
steps.expected: The list of available out-of-band authentication methods does not include 'Email' or 'Email Code'.

steps.action: Initiate a sign-in or sensitive operation that requires out-of-band authentication.
steps.expected: The system presents out-of-band options (e.g., SMS, Authenticator App) but does not offer an option to receive a code via email.

test_cases.title: System rejects email-based out-of-band authentication requests
test_cases.preconditions: A user account exists. Access to the backend API or a way to simulate a client request specifying email as the OOB method is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A request payload specifying 'email' as the out-of-band authentication channel.
test_cases.assumptions: The system exposes an API or internal mechanism where the OOB channel can be explicitly selected or forced for testing purposes.

steps.action: Send a request to initiate out-of-band authentication explicitly specifying 'email' as the delivery channel.
steps.expected: The system rejects the request with an error indicating that email is not a supported or allowed out-of-band authentication method.

steps.action: Verify that no email containing an authentication code was sent to the user's registered email address.
steps.expected: No authentication email is delivered.

test_cases.title: SMS one-time code accepted only once during validity period
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with SMS bound as a second factor to a verified test telephone number. Access to the test telephone number to receive the SMS code.

steps.action: Initiate an authentication transaction for the company representative and request an SMS one-time code.
steps.expected: VBP sends an SMS one-time code to the registered telephone number.

steps.action: Submit the received SMS one-time code in the first authentication transaction.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the code and completes the authentication successfully.

steps.action: Initiate a second authentication transaction for the same account and submit the same SMS one-time code while it is still within its validity period.
steps.expected: VBP rejects the code as invalid or already used.

test_cases.title: Generating a new SMS code does not reset the failed authentication count
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with SMS bound as the second factor. The account has a non-zero failed authentication count (e.g., 1 failed attempt recorded).
test_cases.assumptions: The tester can observe the current failed authentication count via the system's administrative interface or logs.

steps.action: Record the current failed authentication count for the account.
steps.expected: The count is greater than 0.

steps.action: Initiate a sign-in attempt and request a new SMS one-time code.
steps.expected: A new SMS code is sent to the registered telephone number.

steps.action: Check the failed authentication count for the account.
steps.expected: The failed authentication count remains unchanged from the value recorded in step 1.

test_cases.title: Password with only lowercase letters is accepted
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set (activation, change, or recovery).
test_cases.test_inputs: A password of at least 15 characters consisting solely of lowercase ASCII letters, not present in the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of lowercase letters (e.g., 15 'a's or a random lowercase string) that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password with only digits is accepted
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set (activation, change, or recovery).
test_cases.test_inputs: A password of at least 15 characters consisting solely of digits, not present in the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of digits (e.g., 15 '1's or a random numeric string) that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password with only special characters is accepted
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set (activation, change, or recovery).
test_cases.test_inputs: A password of at least 15 characters consisting solely of special characters (e.g., !@#$%), not present in the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of special characters that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password with only spaces is accepted
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set (activation, change, or recovery).
test_cases.test_inputs: A password of at least 15 characters consisting solely of space characters, not present in the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of space characters (15 or more) that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password length validation with Unicode characters
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set or changed (e.g., activation or password change). The candidate password consists of 15 Unicode characters (e.g., 15 distinct emoji or accented letters) that are not on the blocklist.
test_cases.test_inputs: A 15-character password consisting entirely of Unicode code points (e.g., '🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷' or 'ççççççççççççççç').
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports Unicode input in the password field.

steps.action: Enter a password consisting of exactly 15 Unicode characters (e.g., 15 emoji or accented characters) in the password field.
steps.expected: The system accepts the password as meeting the minimum length requirement of 15 characters.

steps.action: Submit the password for validation.
steps.expected: The password is successfully set or changed, confirming that each Unicode code point was counted as a single character.

test_cases.title: Password length validation with mixed ASCII and Unicode characters
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set or changed. The candidate password consists of 10 ASCII characters and 5 Unicode characters, totaling 15 code points, and is not on the blocklist.
test_cases.test_inputs: A 15-character password mixing ASCII and Unicode (e.g., '1234567890ççççç').

steps.action: Enter a password consisting of 10 ASCII characters and 5 Unicode characters (total 15 code points).
steps.expected: The system accepts the password as meeting the minimum length requirement of 15 characters.

steps.action: Submit the password for validation.
steps.expected: The password is successfully set or changed, confirming that mixed character types are counted correctly by code point.

test_cases.title: Rejection of password with 14 Unicode characters
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set or changed. The candidate password consists of 14 Unicode characters and is not on the blocklist.
test_cases.test_inputs: A 14-character password consisting entirely of Unicode code points (e.g., '🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹🇷🇹').

steps.action: Enter a password consisting of exactly 14 Unicode characters.
steps.expected: The system rejects the password, indicating that it does not meet the minimum length requirement of 15 characters.

steps.action: Attempt to submit the password.
steps.expected: The password is not stored, and the user is prompted to enter a valid password.

test_cases.title: Password hint field is not available during activation
test_cases.preconditions: A new company representative is in the account activation flow.

steps.action: Navigate to the password creation step of the company representative activation process.
steps.expected: The form displays fields for the new password and confirmation, but does not display any field, checkbox, or option to enter or store a password hint.

test_cases.title: Password hint field is not available during password change
test_cases.preconditions: An authenticated company representative is in the password change flow.

steps.action: Navigate to the password change screen for an existing company representative account.
steps.expected: The form displays fields for the current password, new password, and confirmation, but does not display any field, checkbox, or option to enter or store a password hint.

test_cases.title: Password hint is not accessible on the public sign-in page
test_cases.preconditions: The user is not authenticated (unauthenticated claimant).

steps.action: Open the public sign-in page of the portal in a browser without logging in.
steps.expected: The page displays the username and password fields, but does not display any link, button, or text that reveals or allows access to a stored password hint for any account.

test_cases.title: Password selection flow does not include security questions
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in the password creation or change state.

steps.action: Initiate the password selection process for a company representative.
steps.expected: The interface displays fields for entering a new password and confirming it, but does not display any knowledge-based authentication questions or security questions (e.g., 'What was the name of your first pet?').

steps.action: Enter a valid password that meets length and blocklist requirements and submit the form.
steps.expected: The password is accepted without requiring answers to any security questions.

test_cases.title: Verification of a long password without truncation
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a known password of at least 64 characters that is not on the blocklist.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid password of 64 characters.

steps.action: Log in to the VBP portal using the company representative's username and the full 64-character password.
steps.expected: The system accepts the login and establishes a session, confirming that the entire password was verified without truncation.

test_cases.title: Rejection of a truncated password
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a known password of at least 64 characters.
test_cases.test_inputs: The first 32 characters of the valid 64-character password.

steps.action: Attempt to log in using the company representative's username and only the first 32 characters of the valid password.
steps.expected: The system rejects the login attempt, indicating that the password is incorrect, thereby confirming that the system does not verify a subset of the password.

test_cases.title: Blocklisted password rejection during establishment
test_cases.preconditions: A new company representative account is being created (activation step). The blocklist contains a known compromised password of at least 15 characters.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid username and a password that is on the blocklist (e.g., a common breached password) and meets the minimum length requirement.

steps.action: Submit a password that is present in the blocklist during the account activation process.
steps.expected: The system rejects the password and does not create the account with that password.

test_cases.title: Blocklisted password rejection during change
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account exists. The user is authenticated and on the password change screen. The blocklist contains a known compromised password of at least 15 characters.
test_cases.test_inputs: The current valid password and a new password that is on the blocklist and meets the minimum length requirement.

steps.action: Submit a new password that is present in the blocklist during the password change process.
steps.expected: The system rejects the new password and the account password remains unchanged.

test_cases.title: Acceptance of non-blocklisted password
test_cases.preconditions: A new company representative account is being created (activation step). A candidate password is known not to be in the blocklist and meets the minimum length requirement.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid username and a strong password that is not on the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit a password that is not present in the blocklist during the account activation process.
steps.expected: The system accepts the password and the account is created successfully.

test_cases.title: Entire password matches blocklist entry
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account exists. A known compromised password of at least 15 characters is present in the VBP blocklist.
test_cases.test_inputs: A password that is an exact match to a known compromised password in the blocklist (length >= 15).

steps.action: Attempt to change the representative's password to the known compromised password that is an exact match to a blocklist entry.
steps.expected: VBP rejects the password and indicates that it is on the blocklist.

test_cases.title: Password contains blocklist word but is not an exact match
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account exists. A common word (e.g., 'password') is in the blocklist. A candidate password contains this word as a substring but is not an exact match to any blocklist entry and meets the length requirement (>= 15 characters).
test_cases.test_inputs: A password of at least 15 characters that contains a blocklisted word as a substring (e.g., 'MySecurePassword123!') but is not itself in the blocklist.
test_cases.assumptions: The blocklist contains the word 'password' but not the specific candidate string 'MySecurePassword123!'.

steps.action: Attempt to change the representative's password to a string that contains a blocklisted word as a substring but is not an exact match to any blocklist entry.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the password, as the comparison is performed on the entire string, not substrings.

test_cases.title: Password is a derivative of a blocklist entry
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account exists. A common password (e.g., '123456789012345') is in the blocklist. A candidate password is a slight modification (e.g., '123456789012345!') that is not an exact match to the blocklist entry but meets the length requirement.
test_cases.test_inputs: A password that is a trivial modification of a blocklisted password (e.g., adding a special character to a known weak password) and is not an exact match to any blocklist entry.
test_cases.assumptions: The blocklist does not contain the modified string '123456789012345!'.

steps.action: Attempt to change the representative's password to a trivial modification of a blocklisted password that is not an exact match to any blocklist entry.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the password, as the requirement specifies comparison of the entire prospective password, not substrings or words, and the exact string is not in the blocklist.

test_cases.title: Rejection of blocklisted password with reason
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account is available for password change. A candidate password of at least 15 characters that is known to be on the blocklist (e.g., a common breached password) is prepared.

steps.action: Attempt to change the company representative's password to the blocklisted candidate password.
steps.expected: VBP rejects the password change request.

steps.action: Observe the error message displayed to the user.
steps.expected: The message states the reason for the rejection (e.g., 'password is too common' or 'password is on the blocklist').

steps.action: Attempt to change the password to a different, non-blocklisted password that meets the length requirement.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the new password and the change is successful.

test_cases.title: Rejection of context-specific blocklisted password with reason
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account is available for password change. A candidate password of at least 15 characters containing context-specific words (e.g., derivatives of the service name 'VatandasBasvuruPortali' or the username) that are on the blocklist is prepared.

steps.action: Attempt to change the company representative's password to the context-specific blocklisted candidate password.
steps.expected: VBP rejects the password change request.

steps.action: Observe the error message displayed to the user.
steps.expected: The message states the reason for the rejection, indicating the password is not allowed (e.g., 'password contains common or context-specific words').

test_cases.title: Guidance displayed after blocklist rejection
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account is at the password change or activation step. A password known to be on the blocklist (e.g., a common breached password) is available for testing.
test_cases.test_inputs: A password that is on the blocklist and meets the minimum length requirement.

steps.action: Enter a password that is on the blocklist and submit it.
steps.expected: The system rejects the password and displays a message indicating the reason for rejection (e.g., 'password is too common' or 'password is compromised').

steps.action: Observe the interface immediately following the rejection message.
steps.expected: Guidance on choosing a strong password is displayed to the representative. The guidance should be specific to the context of the rejection (e.g., suggesting a longer password, avoiding common words, or using a password manager).

test_cases.title: Guidance displayed during initial password setup
test_cases.preconditions: A new company representative account is being activated for the first time.

steps.action: Navigate to the password creation screen during account activation.
steps.expected: The interface displays general guidance on choosing a strong password (e.g., minimum length, character variety, or recommendation to use a password manager) before or while the user is entering the password.

test_cases.title: Password manager autofill functionality is supported on password entry pages
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a known password. A password manager is installed and configured in the test browser.
test_cases.assumptions: The password manager is capable of autofilling standard HTML password fields.

steps.action: Navigate to the company representative login page.
steps.expected: The password input field is present and accessible.

steps.action: Trigger the password manager's autofill feature for the password field.
steps.expected: The password manager successfully populates the password field with the stored credential.

steps.action: Submit the login form.
steps.expected: The system accepts the autofilled password and the user is authenticated successfully.

test_cases.title: Password manager autofill functionality is supported on password change pages
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative is logged in. A password manager is installed and configured in the test browser.
test_cases.assumptions: The password manager can generate or retrieve a new password for the 'new password' field.

steps.action: Navigate to the 'Change Password' page for the company representative account.
steps.expected: Fields for current password, new password, and confirm new password are displayed.

steps.action: Trigger the password manager's autofill or generation feature for the 'new password' field.
steps.expected: The password manager populates the 'new password' field (and potentially 'confirm new password' if supported) with a valid string.

steps.action: Enter the current password manually or via autofill and submit the form.
steps.expected: The password change is successful, and the new password from the manager is accepted.

test_cases.title: Recovery of AAL2 account using two recovery codes from different methods
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account configured for AAL2 authentication. The account has a saved recovery code and a recovery contact configured. The account is in a state requiring recovery (e.g., locked or password forgotten).
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid saved recovery code, valid recovery contact verification (e.g., code sent to contact).

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the AAL2 account.
steps.expected: The system presents options for recovery methods, including the use of recovery codes and recovery contacts.

steps.action: Provide the valid saved recovery code as the first recovery factor.
steps.expected: The system accepts the first recovery code and prompts for a second recovery method from a different source (e.g., recovery contact).

steps.action: Provide the valid recovery code sent to the recovery contact as the second recovery factor.
steps.expected: The system accepts the second recovery code, verifies that the two codes were obtained from different methods, and completes the account recovery process.

test_cases.title: Recovery of AAL2 account using one recovery code and a bound single-factor authenticator
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account configured for AAL2 authentication. The account has a saved recovery code and a bound single-factor authenticator (e.g., password or TOTP). The account is in a state requiring recovery.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid saved recovery code, valid single-factor authenticator credentials (e.g., correct password).

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the AAL2 account.
steps.expected: The system presents options for recovery methods.

steps.action: Provide the valid saved recovery code as the first recovery factor.
steps.expected: The system accepts the recovery code and prompts for authentication with a bound single-factor authenticator.

steps.action: Authenticate using the bound single-factor authenticator (e.g., enter the correct password).
steps.expected: The system accepts the single-factor authentication, verifies the combination, and completes the account recovery process.

test_cases.title: Recovery of AAL2 account using repeated identity proofing
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account configured for AAL2 authentication that has previously undergone identity proofing. The account is in a state requiring recovery.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid identity proofing documents and biometric data (if applicable) matching the initial proofing.
test_cases.assumptions: The system supports repeated identity proofing for AAL2 accounts as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §4.2.2.2.

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the AAL2 account and select the repeated identity proofing option.
steps.expected: The system initiates the identity proofing workflow.

steps.action: Complete the identity proofing process by providing valid identity documents and passing any required biometric or verification checks.
steps.expected: The system verifies the identity proofing and completes the account recovery process.

test_cases.title: Recovery of AAL2 account fails with two recovery codes from the same method
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account configured for AAL2 authentication. The account has two saved recovery codes available. The account is in a state requiring recovery.
test_cases.test_inputs: Two valid saved recovery codes.

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the AAL2 account.
steps.expected: The system presents options for recovery methods.

steps.action: Provide the first valid saved recovery code.
steps.expected: The system accepts the first recovery code and prompts for a second recovery method.

steps.action: Provide the second valid saved recovery code (from the same 'saved' method).
steps.expected: The system rejects the recovery attempt because both codes were obtained from the same method, and the account remains in a state requiring recovery.

test_cases.title: Recovery of AAL2 account fails with one recovery code and incorrect single-factor authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account configured for AAL2 authentication. The account has a saved recovery code and a bound single-factor authenticator (e.g., password). The account is in a state requiring recovery.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid saved recovery code, incorrect single-factor authenticator credentials (e.g., wrong password).

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the AAL2 account.
steps.expected: The system presents options for recovery methods.

steps.action: Provide the valid saved recovery code as the first recovery factor.
steps.expected: The system accepts the recovery code and prompts for authentication with a bound single-factor authenticator.

steps.action: Attempt to authenticate using the bound single-factor authenticator with incorrect credentials (e.g., wrong password).
steps.expected: The system rejects the authentication attempt, and the account recovery process fails or is aborted.

test_cases.title: Disabling multiple authenticators when both reach the failure threshold
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account at AAL2 with a password and a second factor (e.g., TOTP) bound. The failure threshold is 50 consecutive attempts per authenticator.

steps.action: Make 50 consecutive failed password attempts on the account.
steps.expected: The password authenticator is disabled.

steps.action: Make 50 consecutive failed second-factor (TOTP) attempts on the same account.
steps.expected: The second-factor authenticator is disabled.

steps.action: Attempt to sign in using the correct password and a valid TOTP code.
steps.expected: Authentication fails; neither authenticator is accepted because both are disabled.

test_cases.title: Disabling only the authenticator that reaches the threshold
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account at AAL2 with a password and a second factor (e.g., TOTP) bound. The failure threshold is 50 consecutive attempts per authenticator.

steps.action: Make 50 consecutive failed password attempts on the account.
steps.expected: The password authenticator is disabled.

steps.action: Make 10 consecutive failed second-factor (TOTP) attempts on the same account.
steps.expected: The second-factor authenticator remains active.

steps.action: Attempt to sign in using the correct password and a valid TOTP code.
steps.expected: Authentication fails because the password authenticator is disabled, even though the second factor is valid and active.

test_cases.title: Disabled authenticator requires re-binding before use
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a password and a TOTP authenticator bound. The failed-attempt threshold is 50. The account is not currently locked or disabled.

steps.action: Make 50 consecutive failed authentication attempts using the TOTP authenticator on the company representative account, with no successful authentication in between.
steps.expected: The TOTP authenticator is disabled.

steps.action: Attempt to authenticate using the disabled TOTP authenticator with a valid code.
steps.expected: Authentication fails; the system indicates that the authenticator is disabled and must be re-bound.

steps.action: Initiate the re-binding process for the TOTP authenticator, authenticating with the password and any other available valid authenticator as required by the binding process.
steps.expected: The re-binding process is allowed to start.

steps.action: Complete the re-binding process for the TOTP authenticator.
steps.expected: The TOTP authenticator is successfully bound to the account again.

steps.action: Attempt to authenticate using the re-bound TOTP authenticator with a valid code.
steps.expected: Authentication succeeds.

test_cases.title: Disabled password authenticator requires re-binding before use
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a password and a TOTP authenticator bound. The failed-attempt threshold is 50. The account is not currently locked or disabled.

steps.action: Make 50 consecutive failed authentication attempts using the password authenticator on the company representative account, with no successful authentication in between.
steps.expected: The password authenticator is disabled.

steps.action: Attempt to authenticate using the disabled password authenticator with the correct password.
steps.expected: Authentication fails; the system indicates that the password authenticator is disabled and must be re-bound.

steps.action: Initiate the re-binding process for the password authenticator, authenticating with the TOTP authenticator and any other required steps as per the binding process.
steps.expected: The re-binding process is allowed to start.

steps.action: Complete the re-binding process for the password authenticator by setting a new password.
steps.expected: The password authenticator is successfully bound to the account again.

steps.action: Attempt to authenticate using the re-bound password authenticator with the new password.
steps.expected: Authentication succeeds.

test_cases.title: VBP rejects e-Devlet response with AAL below required level
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured to require AAL2 for citizen access. A test e-Devlet IdP (or mock) is available that can issue assertions with a specific 'acr' value below AAL2 (e.g., AAL1).
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid e-Devlet assertion signed with the trusted key, containing an 'acr' value indicating AAL1.
test_cases.assumptions: The 'exception handling' mechanism defined in VBP-YTB-001 §4.2 for insufficient AAL is to open the session in 'limited mode' where personal data is hidden and re-authentication is suggested.

steps.action: Initiate a citizen login via e-Devlet federation.
steps.expected: VBP redirects to the e-Devlet test IdP.

steps.action: The test IdP returns an assertion with an 'acr' value corresponding to AAL1.
steps.expected: VBP validates the signature and other parameters but detects that the AAL is below the required AAL2.

steps.action: Observe the VBP response to the user.
steps.expected: VBP does not grant full access. It routes the user to the exception handling process (limited mode), displaying a message that personal data is not shown and suggesting re-authentication with a stronger method.

test_cases.title: VBP accepts e-Devlet response meeting required IAL, AAL, and FAL
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured to require AAL2 for citizen access. A test e-Devlet IdP (or mock) is available that can issue assertions with a specific 'acr' value meeting AAL2.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid e-Devlet assertion signed with the trusted key, containing an 'acr' value indicating AAL2, valid 'auth_time', and correct 'aud'.

steps.action: Initiate a citizen login via e-Devlet federation.
steps.expected: VBP redirects to the e-Devlet test IdP.

steps.action: The test IdP returns an assertion with an 'acr' value corresponding to AAL2.
steps.expected: VBP validates the signature, audience, and assurance levels.

steps.action: Observe the VBP response to the user.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the assertion and establishes a full session, allowing access to personal data and application content.

test_cases.title: VBP handles missing 'acr' claim in e-Devlet response
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured to require AAL2 for citizen access. A test e-Devlet IdP (or mock) is available that can issue assertions without the 'acr' claim.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid e-Devlet assertion signed with the trusted key, but missing the 'acr' claim.
test_cases.assumptions: According to VBP-YTB-001 §4.2, if the 'acr' field is missing, VBP assumes single-factor authentication and opens the session in 'limited mode'.

steps.action: Initiate a citizen login via e-Devlet federation.
steps.expected: VBP redirects to the e-Devlet test IdP.

steps.action: The test IdP returns an assertion that does not contain the 'acr' claim.
steps.expected: VBP validates the signature but detects the missing assurance level indicator.

steps.action: Observe the VBP response to the user.
steps.expected: VBP treats the session as having insufficient assurance (single-factor) and routes the user to the exception handling process (limited mode), hiding personal data and suggesting re-authentication.

test_cases.title: Session AAL does not exceed the authentication event AAL
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen account capable of AAL1 (password only) and AAL2 (password + second factor) authentication. Access to inspect session attributes (e.g., via API response headers or debug endpoint) to verify the assigned AAL.
test_cases.assumptions: The system exposes the current session AAL level in a verifiable manner (e.g., header, cookie, or API field).

steps.action: Authenticate as a citizen using only the password (AAL1).
steps.expected: The session is established and the session AAL is recorded as AAL1.

steps.action: Access a protected resource that requires AAL2.
steps.expected: Access is denied or the user is prompted to upgrade authentication; the session AAL remains AAL1 and does not automatically become AAL2.

steps.action: Authenticate as a citizen using password and second factor (AAL2).
steps.expected: The session is established and the session AAL is recorded as AAL2.

steps.action: Access a protected resource that requires AAL1.
steps.expected: Access is granted; the session AAL remains AAL2 (treating at a lower AAL is permitted).

test_cases.title: Session AAL cannot be escalated without re-authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active citizen session established at AAL1 (password only).
test_cases.assumptions: The system exposes the current session AAL level in a verifiable manner.

steps.action: While in an AAL1 session, attempt to access a resource that requires AAL2 by directly requesting the URL or API endpoint.
steps.expected: The request is rejected or redirected to the AAL2 authentication flow; the session AAL is not upgraded to AAL2 without completing the second-factor step.

steps.action: Complete the AAL2 authentication flow (second factor) from the AAL1 session.
steps.expected: The session AAL is updated to AAL2 only after successful second-factor verification.

test_cases.title: Authenticated session does not fall back to HTTP
test_cases.preconditions: A valid user account exists. The user is authenticated via HTTPS.

steps.action: Authenticate as a user via the HTTPS endpoint.
steps.expected: Authentication is successful and an active session is established over HTTPS.

steps.action: Attempt to access a protected resource using the same session cookie/token but via an HTTP URL (insecure transport).
steps.expected: The request is rejected or redirected to HTTPS; the session is not accepted over the insecure HTTP connection.

test_cases.title: Session remains valid over HTTPS after initial authentication
test_cases.preconditions: A valid user account exists.

steps.action: Authenticate as a user via the HTTPS endpoint.
steps.expected: Authentication is successful.

steps.action: Access a protected resource using the session via an HTTPS URL.
steps.expected: The resource is served successfully, confirming the session is active and valid over the secure transport.

test_cases.title: Bot detection blocks automated proofing attempts
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with the company representative proofing flow accessible. A script or tool capable of simulating automated bot traffic (e.g., headless browser or HTTP client without human-like behavior) is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: Automated request payload simulating a bot attempting to initiate the proofing process.
test_cases.assumptions: The system's bot detection mechanism is configured to block or challenge non-human traffic.

steps.action: Initiate the company representative identity proofing process using an automated script that mimics bot behavior (e.g., missing browser headers, rapid sequential requests, or known bot signatures).
steps.expected: The system detects the automated attack and blocks the request or presents a challenge (e.g., CAPTCHA) that prevents the automated process from proceeding.

steps.action: Verify the system logs or security dashboard for the attempt.
steps.expected: The attempt is logged as a blocked automated attack or bot detection event.

test_cases.title: Web Application Firewall (WAF) blocks malicious input in proofing forms
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with the company representative proofing flow accessible. The WAF is active and configured to block common web attacks.
test_cases.test_inputs: A form submission containing a known SQL injection or Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) payload in a text field of the proofing form.
test_cases.assumptions: The WAF rules are configured to detect and block SQLi and XSS patterns.

steps.action: Submit the company representative proofing form with a field containing a malicious SQL injection string (e.g., ' OR 1=1 --).
steps.expected: The WAF intercepts the request and returns a block page or error response, preventing the payload from reaching the application backend.

steps.action: Submit the form with a field containing a malicious XSS script (e.g., <script>alert('xss')</script>).
steps.expected: The WAF intercepts the request and blocks the submission, preventing the script from being stored or executed.

test_cases.title: Behavioral analytics flags abnormal user behavior during proofing
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with behavioral analytics enabled for the proofing process. A user account or session capable of generating abnormal behavior patterns is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A sequence of user actions that deviate significantly from normal human behavior (e.g., extremely fast form completion, mouse movement patterns inconsistent with human input, or access from multiple geographically distant IPs in a short time).
test_cases.assumptions: The behavioral analytics engine is configured to flag high-risk indicators such as rapid input or impossible travel.

steps.action: Simulate a user completing the proofing form with superhuman speed (e.g., filling all fields in less than 1 second) or using a tool that generates non-human mouse/keyboard events.
steps.expected: The behavioral analytics system flags the session as high-risk or suspicious.

steps.action: Check the security monitoring interface or logs for the flagged session.
steps.expected: The session is marked with a high-risk indicator due to abnormal behavioral patterns, and appropriate mitigation actions (e.g., step-up authentication or block) are triggered or logged.

test_cases.title: Network traffic analysis identifies and blocks high-risk IP addresses
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with network traffic analysis enabled. Access to a proxy or IP address that is on a known blocklist of high-risk or malicious IPs.
test_cases.test_inputs: A request to the company representative proofing endpoint originating from a known high-risk or blocklisted IP address.
test_cases.assumptions: The network traffic analysis component maintains an up-to-date list of high-risk IPs and is configured to block or challenge traffic from them.

steps.action: Initiate the company representative proofing process from a client configured to use a known high-risk or blocklisted IP address.
steps.expected: The network traffic analysis system identifies the source IP as high-risk and blocks the connection or presents a challenge.

steps.action: Verify the network logs for the blocked connection.
steps.expected: The log entry indicates that the request was blocked due to the source IP being on the high-risk/blocklist.

test_cases.title: TOTP code is rejected upon second submission within validity window
test_cases.preconditions: An active user account with TOTP bound as the second factor. The tester has access to the TOTP authenticator app and can generate valid codes.

steps.action: Initiate the login process and enter valid credentials for the first factor.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second factor (TOTP code).

steps.action: Generate a TOTP code from the authenticator app and submit it to complete the login.
steps.expected: The login is successful and the user is authenticated.

steps.action: Log out of the system.
steps.expected: The session is terminated.

steps.action: Initiate a new login process with the same user credentials.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second factor (TOTP code).

steps.action: Submit the exact same TOTP code that was used in step 2, ensuring it is still within its 30-second validity window (or the 59-second acceptance window defined in the design).
steps.expected: The system rejects the TOTP code and displays an error message indicating the code is invalid or already used.

test_cases.title: Replacement saved recovery code issuance triggers account recovery notification
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a registered non-postal notification address (e.g., e-mail) that the tester can access. The representative is authenticated in a session that allows account management actions.

steps.action: Request a replacement for the current saved recovery code from the account management interface.
steps.expected: The system issues a new saved recovery code and invalidates the previous one.

steps.action: Check the registered notification address (e.g., e-mail inbox) for a message.
steps.expected: An account recovery notification is received, indicating that a recovery code replacement has occurred.

test_cases.title: Invalidation of used saved recovery code and issuance of new code
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a valid saved recovery code. The tester has access to the account's notification channel to verify the new code issuance.
test_cases.test_inputs: The current valid saved recovery code.

steps.action: Initiate the account recovery process for the company representative and submit the current valid saved recovery code.
steps.expected: The recovery process is successful, and the account is recovered.

steps.action: Check the notification channel (e.g., email or portal message) associated with the account.
steps.expected: A new saved recovery code is issued to the company representative.

steps.action: Attempt to use the original saved recovery code (the one used in step 1) in a new recovery attempt for the same account.
steps.expected: The system rejects the code as invalid or already used.

test_cases.title: Accessing account information with valid AAL2 authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a password and a second factor (e.g., TOTP) bound. The representative is not currently authenticated.

steps.action: Initiate sign-in as the company representative using the correct password.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second authentication factor.

steps.action: Provide the correct second factor (e.g., TOTP code).
steps.expected: Authentication completes successfully at AAL2.

steps.action: Navigate to a page containing personal information in the subscriber account.
steps.expected: The personal information is displayed and accessible.

test_cases.title: Accessing account information with valid AAL3 authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account configured for AAL3 with a phishing-resistant authenticator (e.g., passkey) and a password/activation factor bound.

steps.action: Initiate sign-in as the company representative using the AAL3 authentication flow (e.g., passkey prompt).
steps.expected: The system verifies the possession of the key and the activation factor/password.

steps.action: Complete the AAL3 authentication successfully.
steps.expected: Authentication completes successfully at AAL3.

steps.action: Navigate to a page containing personal information in the subscriber account.
steps.expected: The personal information is displayed and accessible.

test_cases.title: Attempting to access account information with only AAL1 authentication
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a password and a second factor bound. The representative is not currently authenticated.

steps.action: Initiate sign-in as the company representative using the correct password.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second authentication factor.

steps.action: Attempt to bypass the second factor step or terminate the authentication process after only the password is verified (simulating an AAL1-only session if technically possible via direct URL access to protected resources without full MFA completion).
steps.expected: Access to personal information in the account is denied. The system does not establish a session that permits viewing personal data with only the first factor.

test_cases.title: Attempting to access account information with an unregistered authenticator
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a specific TOTP app bound. A different, unregistered TOTP app or passkey is available for testing.

steps.action: Initiate sign-in as the company representative using the correct password.
steps.expected: The system prompts for the second authentication factor.

steps.action: Provide a code from the unregistered TOTP app or attempt to use the unregistered passkey.
steps.expected: Authentication fails. The system does not establish an authenticated session, and access to account information is denied.

test_cases.title: Notification sent upon update of core account information
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account at AAL2 with a registered notification address (e.g., email) that the tester can access. The account has updatable core information (e.g., phone number or email address).
test_cases.test_inputs: A new valid value for a core attribute (e.g., a new phone number).

steps.action: Sign in as the company representative and navigate to the account settings.
steps.expected: The account settings page is displayed with the current core information.

steps.action: Update a core attribute (e.g., change the phone number) to a new valid value and save the changes.
steps.expected: The system validates the change and confirms the update on the screen.

steps.action: Check the registered notification address (e.g., email inbox) for a notification regarding the account update.
steps.expected: A notification is received informing the representative that their account information has been updated.

test_cases.title: Notification sent upon update of non-core account information
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account at AAL2 with a registered notification address that the tester can access. The account has updatable non-core information (e.g., preferred language or display name) that can be updated directly by the subscriber.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new value for a non-core attribute (e.g., a new display name).

steps.action: Sign in as the company representative and navigate to the account settings.
steps.expected: The account settings page is displayed.

steps.action: Update a non-core attribute (e.g., change the display name) and save the changes.
steps.expected: The system accepts the change and confirms the update.

steps.action: Check the registered notification address for a notification regarding the account update.
steps.expected: A notification is received informing the representative that their account information has been updated.

test_cases.title: Reporting unauthorized access via the account interface
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account at AAL2, authenticated within the last 5 minutes, with access to the account dashboard.

steps.action: Navigate to the company representative account settings or security page.
steps.expected: A visible option or link to report unauthorized access or potential compromise is present.

steps.action: Select the option to report unauthorized access or potential compromise.
steps.expected: A form or interface is displayed allowing the representative to describe the incident or confirm the report.

steps.action: Submit the report with a brief description of the suspected compromise.
steps.expected: The system confirms that the report has been received and logged.

test_cases.title: Reporting potential compromise of account information
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account at AAL2, authenticated within the last 5 minutes.

steps.action: Access the account security or help section.
steps.expected: A mechanism to report potential compromise of information in the account is available.

steps.action: Initiate a report for potential compromise of personal information stored in the account.
steps.expected: The system accepts the report and provides a confirmation message or reference number.

test_cases.title: Generic error message on unexpected server error
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment where an internal server error (e.g., 500) can be triggered, such as by accessing a malformed URL or simulating a backend failure.
test_cases.test_inputs: A request that triggers an internal server error (e.g., invalid parameter causing a 500).

steps.action: Send a request to the portal that triggers an unexpected internal server error.
steps.expected: The response body contains a generic error message (e.g., 'An unexpected error occurred') and does not contain stack traces, SQL queries, secret keys, tokens, or version numbers.

steps.action: Inspect the HTTP response headers and body for sensitive internal details.
steps.expected: No internal system details such as server version, framework version, or database connection strings are exposed in the response.

test_cases.title: Generic error message on security-sensitive error
test_cases.preconditions: A valid user account and a way to trigger a security-sensitive error, such as an authorization failure or a failed external dependency call that results in an error.
test_cases.test_inputs: A request that triggers a security-sensitive error (e.g., accessing a resource without permission or a failed external API call).

steps.action: Trigger a security-sensitive error, such as attempting to access a resource without proper authorization or causing a failure in an external dependency.
steps.expected: The response body contains a generic error message and does not expose internal details such as stack traces, queries, secret keys, or tokens.

steps.action: Verify that the error message does not reveal the specific cause of the security-sensitive error in a way that could be exploited.
steps.expected: The message is generic and does not provide information that could help an attacker understand the system's internal structure or security mechanisms.

test_cases.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute and is set via Set-Cookie header
test_cases.preconditions: A valid user account exists. An intercepting proxy or browser developer tools are available to inspect HTTP headers and cookies.

steps.action: Sign in to the portal with valid credentials.
steps.expected: The response contains a 'Set-Cookie' header for the session cookie. The cookie attributes include 'HttpOnly'. The session token value is not present in the HTML body or JavaScript variables.

steps.action: Inspect the session cookie in the browser's cookie store or via the proxy.
steps.expected: The session cookie is marked as HttpOnly, preventing access via document.cookie in client-side scripts.

test_cases.title: Non-session cookies not meant for scripts have HttpOnly attribute
test_cases.preconditions: The portal sets at least one non-session cookie that is not intended to be accessible to client-side scripts (e.g., a CSRF token cookie or a security-related flag).
test_cases.assumptions: The specific non-session cookie name is identified from the VBP Software Design Document or code review.

steps.action: Trigger the action that sets the non-session cookie (e.g., load a page that sets a CSRF token cookie).
steps.expected: The 'Set-Cookie' header for this cookie includes the 'HttpOnly' attribute.

steps.action: Attempt to read the cookie value using client-side JavaScript (e.g., document.cookie).
steps.expected: The cookie value is not accessible via JavaScript.

test_cases.title: HSTS header present on all responses with correct max-age and subdomain coverage
test_cases.preconditions: Access to the portal via HTTPS. The VBP Software Design Document §14 specifies the required max-age and subdomain coverage (e.g., max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains).
test_cases.assumptions: The required max-age is at least 1 year (31536000 seconds) and includeSubDomains is required, as per OWASP ASVS V3.4.1 L2+ and typical SDD specifications.

steps.action: Send an HTTPS request to the main portal URL.
steps.expected: The response includes a 'Strict-Transport-Security' header. The header value includes 'max-age' with a value of at least 31536000 and 'includeSubDomains'.

steps.action: Send an HTTPS request to a subdomain of the portal (if applicable) or a different path.
steps.expected: The response includes the 'Strict-Transport-Security' header with the same max-age and includeSubDomains directives.

steps.action: Send an HTTPS request to a static asset (e.g., CSS or JS file).
steps.expected: The response includes the 'Strict-Transport-Security' header with the correct max-age and includeSubDomains directives.

test_cases.title: HSTS header present on error responses
test_cases.preconditions: Access to the portal via HTTPS.

steps.action: Send an HTTPS request to a non-existent resource to trigger a 404 error.
steps.expected: The 404 response includes a 'Strict-Transport-Security' header with the correct max-age and includeSubDomains directives.

steps.action: Send an HTTPS request that triggers a 500 server error (if possible in test environment).
steps.expected: The 500 response includes a 'Strict-Transport-Security' header with the correct max-age and includeSubDomains directives.

test_cases.title: Valid file upload with matching extension and content
test_cases.preconditions: User is signed in and has permission to upload files. A valid PDF file with a .pdf extension is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid PDF file named 'document.pdf'.

steps.action: Upload the valid PDF file 'document.pdf' through the file upload interface.
steps.expected: The file is accepted and the upload is successful.

test_cases.title: File upload with mismatched extension and content
test_cases.preconditions: User is signed in and has permission to upload files. A file with a .pdf extension but containing executable content (e.g., a renamed .exe file) is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A file named 'malicious.pdf' that actually contains executable code.

steps.action: Upload the file 'malicious.pdf' which has a .pdf extension but contains executable content.
steps.expected: The upload is rejected with an error message indicating that the file content does not match the extension.

test_cases.title: File upload with unexpected extension
test_cases.preconditions: User is signed in and has permission to upload files. A file with an extension not in the allowed list (e.g., .sh) is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A shell script file named 'script.sh'.

steps.action: Upload the file 'script.sh' which has an extension not in the allowed list.
steps.expected: The upload is rejected with an error message indicating that the file extension is not allowed.

test_cases.title: Image upload within maximum pixel size
test_cases.preconditions: User is signed in and has permission to upload images. A valid image file with pixel dimensions below the maximum defined in VBP Software Design Document §14 is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid image file with dimensions below the maximum allowed size.
test_cases.assumptions: The maximum pixel size is defined in VBP Software Design Document §14.

steps.action: Upload the valid image file with dimensions below the maximum allowed size.
steps.expected: The image is accepted and the upload is successful.

test_cases.title: Image upload exceeding maximum pixel size
test_cases.preconditions: User is signed in and has permission to upload images. A valid image file with pixel dimensions exceeding the maximum defined in VBP Software Design Document §14 is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: A valid image file with dimensions exceeding the maximum allowed size.
test_cases.assumptions: The maximum pixel size is defined in VBP Software Design Document §14.

steps.action: Upload the valid image file with dimensions exceeding the maximum allowed size.
steps.expected: The upload is rejected with an error message indicating that the image pixel size exceeds the maximum allowed.

test_cases.title: Failed sign-in responses do not reveal user existence
test_cases.preconditions: A valid registered user account and an unregistered user identifier are available for testing.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid user credentials, invalid user credentials, unregistered user identifier.

steps.action: Attempt sign-in with a valid user identifier and an incorrect password.
steps.expected: The system returns a generic error message (e.g., 'Invalid credentials') and an HTTP 401 status code.

steps.action: Attempt sign-in with an unregistered user identifier and an arbitrary password.
steps.expected: The system returns the same generic error message and HTTP 401 status code as in step 1.

steps.action: Compare the response time of the failed sign-in for the valid user (step 1) and the unregistered user (step 2).
steps.expected: The response times are statistically indistinguishable, preventing user enumeration via timing attacks.

test_cases.title: Registration and forgotten-password responses do not reveal user existence
test_cases.preconditions: A valid registered user email address and an unregistered email address are available for testing.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid registered email, unregistered email.

steps.action: Submit a registration request with an already registered email address.
steps.expected: The system returns a generic response (e.g., 'Registration request processed' or 'Check your email') without explicitly stating the email is already in use, and returns a standard HTTP status code (e.g., 200 or 202).

steps.action: Submit a registration request with an unregistered email address.
steps.expected: The system returns the same generic response and HTTP status code as in step 1.

steps.action: Submit a forgotten-password request for a valid registered email address.
